examples.en: There's really no way to continue this conversation any longer.
examples.zh: 这场谈话真是无法再进行下去了。

examples.en: Sami and Layla have a long conversation to finish.
examples.zh: 萨米和蕾拉还有很多话要谈。

conversion.definition:
n. an event that results in a transformation
n. a change in the units or form of an expression: "conversion from Fahrenheit to Centigrade"
n. a successful free throw or try for point after a touchdown
n. a spiritual enlightenment causing a person to lead a new life
conversion.translation: n. 转变, 转换, 改变宗教信仰, 换位法\n[计] 转换

examples.en: Sami's conversion to Islam was a life-changing thing.
examples.zh: 萨米皈依伊斯兰教对他的人生产生了深远的影响。

examples.en: Conversion therapy is torture.
examples.zh: 扭转治疗是酷刑。

convert.definition:
n. a person who has been converted to another religious or political belief
v. change from one system to another or to a new plan or policy
v. change the nature, purpose, or function of something
v. change religious beliefs, or adopt a religious belief
convert.translation:
n. 皈依者, 改变宗教信仰者
vt. 使改变信仰, 转换, 兑换, 倒置
vi. 皈依
[计] 转换

examples.en: The cells have the capacity to convert food into energy.
examples.zh: 细胞具有将食物转化为能量的能力。

examples.en: He is a recent convert to Catholicism.
examples.zh: 他新近皈依的天主教徒。

examples.en: Tom bought an old ambulance and converted it into a camper.
examples.zh: 汤姆买了一辆旧救护车，并把它改装成露营车。

convey.definition: v. make known; pass on, of information\nv. transfer to another\nv. transmit a title or property
convey.translation: vt. 传达, 运输, 转让\n[经] 转让(财产等), 搬运

examples.en: His words convey nothing at all to me.
examples.zh: 他的话对我来说没有任何意义。

examples.en: Wires are used to convey electricity.
examples.zh: 电线被用来运送电力。

examples.en: While dreams cannot tell you what will happen to you in reality, they are able to convey your innermost thoughts.
examples.zh: 梦虽然不会告诉你现实中将要发生什么，却能告诉你内心的真实想法。

convict.definition: n. a person serving a sentence in a jail or prison\nn. a person who has been convicted of a criminal offense\nv. find or declare guilty
convict.translation: n. 囚犯, 罪犯\nvt. 宣告有罪, 使知罪

examples.en: The police are hunting an escaped convict in this area.
There wasn't enough evidence to convict him of the crime.
Tom found the evidence we needed to convict Mary's killer.

conviction.definition: n. an unshakable belief in something without need for proof or evidence\nn. (criminal law) a final judgment of guilty in a criminal case and the punishment that is imposed
conviction.translation: n. 定罪, 信服, 坚信\n[法] 定罪, 证明有罪, 判罪

examples.en: Betty has a previous conviction for theft.
examples.zh: 贝蒂有盗窃前科。

examples.en: One must have conviction in law, or its existence will be superficial only.
examples.zh: 法律必须被信仰，否则形同虚设。

convince.definition: v make (someone) agree, understand, or realize the truth or validity of something
convince.translation: vt. 说服, 使相信\n[法] 使确信, 使信服, 使人认识错误

examples.en: Tom tried to convince Mary to knit him a scarf.
examples.zh: 汤姆想说服玛丽给他织一条围巾。

examples.en: She was asked to convince him to paint the house.
examples.zh: 有人要她去劝他刷房子。

examples.en: She couldn't convince him to write a song for her.
examples.zh: 她没能说服他为她写首歌。

cook.definition:
n. someone who cooks food
n. English navigator who claimed the east coast of Australia for Britain and discovered several Pacific islands (1728-1779)
v. prepare a hot meal
v. prepare for eating by applying heat
cook.translation: n. 厨子, 厨师\nvt. 烹调, 煮饭, 加热\nvi. 在煮着

examples.en: Daddy must be able to cook at least one egg!
examples.zh: 当爸爸的必须至少会煮蛋。

examples.en: She says to the cook: Thank you for the meals.
examples.zh: 她对厨师说: 谢谢您做的饭菜。

examples.en: Tom can't cook very well, so he often eats out.
examples.zh: 汤姆不怎么会烧饭所以他经常出去吃。

cookie.definition: n. any of various small flat sweet cakes (`biscuit' is the British term)\nn. the cook on a ranch or at a camp\nn. a short line of text that a web site puts on your computer's hard drive when you access the web site
cookie.translation: n. 饼干, 小甜点\n[建] 糕点

examples.en: I think Cookie got into something he wasn't supposed to.
examples.zh: 我觉得曲奇卷入了不该卷入的事。

examples.en: Tom thought Cookie would be a good name for his dog.
examples.zh: 汤姆认为“小饼干”这个名字很适合他的狗。

examples.en: "Has Cookie been acting weird lately?" "He's a cat."
examples.zh: 「曲奇最近行为怪异吗？」「他是一只猫。」

cool.definition:
n. the quality of being at a refreshingly low temperature
v. make cool or cooler
v. loose heat
v. lose intensity
cool.translation:
n. 凉爽, 凉爽的空气
a. 凉爽的, 冷淡的, 冷静的
vi. 冷却, 平息
vt. 使冷却, 使平静

examples.en: I was quite thirsty and wanted to drink something cool.
examples.zh: 我很渴，想喝点冷饮。

examples.en: Do you think of me as a cool guy?
examples.zh: 你觉得我是个酷哥吗？

examples.en: It's easy to err once you lose your cool.
examples.zh: 一急容易出乱子。

cooperate.definition: v work together on a common enterprise of project
cooperate.translation: vi. 合作, 协力, 配合\n[化] 合作

examples.en: We are working hard to cooperate more.
examples.zh: 我们正在努力扩展合作。

cooperation.definition: n. joint operation or action\nn. the practice of cooperating
cooperation.translation: n. 合作, 协力, 配合\n[化] 合作

examples.en: Completing this project would require the cooperation of multiple parties.
examples.zh: 这个项目要多方合作才能完成。

examples.en: No one could predict the outcome of this cooperation.
examples.zh: 没人能够预言这次合作的结果。

examples.en: With their cooperation, the mission had been successfully finished.
examples.zh: 在他们的默契合作下，任务完美地完成了。

coordinate.definition:
n. a number that identifies a position relative to an axis
v. bring into common action, movement, or condition
v. be co-ordinated
s. of equal importance, rank, or degree
coordinate.translation: n. 同等的人(或物), 坐标\na. 同等的, 并列的\nv. (使)协调

examples.en: I'll liaise with the marketing team to coordinate the launch.
I had to coordinate the tasks of twenty people.
Don't worry, if that happens, we will just have to coordinate!

cope.definition: n. a long cloak; worn by a priest or bishop on ceremonial occasions\nv. come to terms with
cope.translation: vi. 竞争, 应付\nn. 长袍

examples.en: The problem is how we cope with the present difficulties.
examples.zh: 问题是我们如何应付目前的困难。

examples.en: Tom found Mary's constant criticism of him hard to cope with.
examples.zh: 汤姆认为和经常批评他的玛丽很难相处。

examples.en: We have to cope with hosts of difficulties.
examples.zh: 我们要面对许多的困难。

copy.definition:
n. a thing made to be similar or identical to another thing
n. matter to be printed; exclusive of graphical materials
n. material suitable for a journalistic account
v. copy down as is
copy.translation:
n. 副本, 摹仿, 一册
v. 复印, 抄袭, 复制
[计] 副本; 复制; DOS内部命令:复制文件
将几个文件合并成一个文件, 以及将文件传至外设或在设备之间传送

examples.en: I keep the master copy under lock and key.
examples.zh: 我妥善保管原版拷贝。

examples.en: He is a carbon copy of his father.
examples.zh: 他是他父亲的翻版。

examples.en: Can you please copy me on that email?
examples.zh: 那封邮件可以 CC 我吗？

copyright.definition: n. a document granting exclusive right to publish and sell literary or musical or artistic work\nv. secure a copyright on a written work
copyright.translation: n. 版权, 著作权\n[法] 著作权

examples.en: Tom always violates copyright laws.
examples.zh: 汤姆一向违反知识产权。

examples.en: I wish copyrights didn't last so long.
examples.zh: 我希望版权不用持续这么久。

examples.en: Don't add sentences from copyrighted sources.
examples.zh: 请勿由享有版权的来源添加句子。

cord.definition:
n. a line made of twisted fibers or threads
n. a unit of amount of wood cut for burning; 128 cubic feet
n. a light insulated conductor for household use
n. a cut pile fabric with vertical ribs; usually made of cotton
cord.translation: n. 绳索, 束缚\n[医] 索, 带

examples.en: Is the power cord plugged into a power outlet?
examples.zh: 插头插到插座里了吗？

examples.en: This extension cord is too short.
examples.zh: 这条延长线太短了。

examples.en: I need an extension cord.
examples.zh: 我需要一条延长线。

core.definition:
n. a small group of indispensable persons or things
n. the center of an object
n. the central part of the Earth
n. a cylindrical sample of soil or rock obtained with a hollow drill
core.translation: n. 核心, 果心, 要点\nvt. 挖...的核\n[计] 内核, 核心网

examples.en: My mum helps me remove the core of the plum.
examples.zh: 妈妈帮我把李子去了核。

examples.en: I don't eat the core of an apple.
examples.zh: 我不吃苹果核。

examples.en: He is rotten to the core.
examples.zh: 他坏透了。

corn.definition:
n. tall annual cereal grass bearing kernels on large ears: widely cultivated in America in many varieties; the principal cereal in Mexico and Central and South America since pre-Columbian times
n. the dried grains or kernels or corn used as animal feed or ground for meal
n. ears of corn that can be prepared and served for human food
n. a hard thickening of the skin (especially on the top or sides of the toes) caused by the pressure of ill-fitting shoes
corn.translation: n. 玉蜀黍, 谷类, 谷粒, 鸡眼\nvt. 使成颗粒, 腌

examples.en: What country has the absolute advantage in the production of corn?
examples.zh: 哪一个国家拥有生产玉米的绝对优势？

examples.en: Our breakfast has oats and corn in it.
examples.zh: 我们早餐有燕麦和玉米。

examples.en: I bought a bag of frozen corn.
examples.zh: 我买了一包冰冻玉米。

corner.definition:
n. a place off to the side of an area
n. the point where two lines meet or intersect
n. an interior angle formed by two meeting walls
n. the intersection of two streets
corner.translation:
n. 角落, 转角, 窘境
vt. 迫至一隅, 垄断, 使陷入绝境
vi. 相交成角, 垄断
[计] 边角

examples.en: The girl was sobbing in the corner of the schoolroom.
examples.zh: 女孩在教室的角落啜泣。

examples.en: Tom is standing in the corner of the room.
examples.zh: 汤姆正站在房间的角落。

examples.en: Edmundo hid in the back corner of the bathroom.
examples.zh: 艾德蒙多躲在浴室的角落。

corporate.definition: a. of or belonging to a corporation\ns. done by or characteristic of individuals acting together\ns. organized and maintained as a legal corporation
corporate.translation: a. 社团的, 合伙的, 公司的\n[经] 团体的, 法人的, 社团的

examples.en: Corporate earnings in the first quarter improved sharply.
examples.zh: 企业第一季度收益大幅增长。

corporation.definition: n. a business firm whose articles of incorporation have been approved in some state
corporation.translation: n. 公司, 合作, 法人团体\n[法] 法人团体, 社团, 法人

examples.en: Toyota Corporation announced that it would cut 1,000 positions this year.
examples.zh: 丰田公司宣布将会在今年裁员一千人。

examples.en: The multinational corporation has forecast the implementation of economies of scale.
examples.zh: 跨国公司预料到了规模经济的实行。

examples.en: Multinational corporations outperform traditional corporations operating in just one country.
examples.zh: 跨国企业远胜于传统的单一国家企业。

correct.definition:
v. make right or correct
v. treat a defect
a. free from error; especially conforming to fact or truth
s. socially right or correct
correct.translation: a. 正确的, 合适的\nvt. 改正, 订正

examples.en: Correct the mistake and return the file to Mr Luxemburg.
examples.zh: 请把错误改正过来，然后把文件夹还给 Luxemburg 先生。

examples.en: Correct, one has a stomachache, the other has a headache.
examples.zh: 对，一个人肚子疼，另一个人头疼。

examples.en: The password isn't correct, so try again. Passwords are case-sensitive.
examples.zh: 密码不正确，请再试一次。密码需区分大小写。

correlate.definition: n. either of two or more related or complementary variables\nv. to bear a reciprocal or mutual relation\nv. bring into a mutual, complementary, or reciprocal relation
correlate.translation: n. 有相互关系的东西, 相关物\nvt. 使有相互关系\nvi. 相关

examples.en: I used to correlate love with sex.
Sami doesn't think that these things are correlated.
Some of the work in the workbook doesn't correlate with the readings in the textbook.

correspond.translation: vi. 符合, 通信, 相当\n[法] 符合, 一致, 相当

examples.en: Your words must correspond with your actions.
examples.zh: 你的言行必须一致。

examples.en: What he says always corresponds with what he does.
examples.zh: 他是个表里如一的人。

examples.en: I don't know anyone who corresponds to that description.
examples.zh: 我不认识符合条件的人。

correspondence.definition: n. communication by the exchange of letters
correspondence.translation: n. 相符, 通信, 信件\n[医] 对应, 相对

examples.en: Your correspondence with Tom is not a secret to anyone.
This pair of lovers were carrying on an ardent correspondence.
It's impossible to learn to swim from a correspondence course.

correspondent.definition: n. someone who communicates by means of letters\nn. a journalist employed to provide news stories for newspapers or broadcast media
correspondent.translation: n. 通讯记者, 通信者\n[经] 客户, 代理商行, 代理银行

examples.en: As a war correspondent, Tom visited several war zones.
A correspondent must soon adjust himself to life abroad.
Oleg introduced himself to Rima as a news correspondent.

corresponding.definition: s. accompanying\ns. similar especially in position or purpose
corresponding.translation: a. 相当的, 一致的, 通信的\n[计] 对应

examples.en: I am corresponding with an American high school student.
Wuhan's virology lab has no samples corresponding to COVID.
For every action, there is a corresponding reaction.

corridor.definition: n. an enclosed passageway; rooms usually open onto it
corridor.translation: n. 走廊, 回廊, 人口密集地带

examples.en: Every morning, the corridor was swept clean.
examples.zh: 走廊每天早上都清扫得干干净净。

corrupt.definition:
v. corrupt morally or by intemperance or sensuality
v. alter from the original
a. lacking in integrity
s. containing errors or alterations
corrupt.translation: a. 腐败的, 贪污的, 讹误充斥的\nvt. 使腐烂, 腐蚀, 使恶化\nvi. 腐烂, 堕落

examples.en: Let's chase out corrupt politicians!
examples.zh: 让我们赶走腐败的政客！

examples.en: The file is corrupt.
examples.zh: 文件已损坏。

corruption.definition:
n. decay of matter (as by rot or oxidation)
n. moral perversion; impairment of virtue and moral principles
n. destroying someone's (or some group's) honesty or loyalty; undermining moral integrity
n. inducement (as of a public official) by improper means (as bribery) to violate duty (as by commiting a felony)
corruption.translation: n. 腐败, 堕落, 贪污\n[计] 论误

examples.en: The politician pushed for reform by denouncing the corruption of the government officials.
examples.zh: 政治家以揭露政府官员的腐败来推动改革。

cost.definition: n. the total spent for goods or services including money and time and labor\nv. be priced at\nv. require to lose, suffer, or sacrifice
cost.translation: n. 代价, 价值, 费用\nvi. 花费\nvt. 使失去, 值, 使花费

examples.en: How much will it cost you to go by air?
examples.zh: 坐飞机将花你多少钱？

examples.en: He saved the baby at the cost of his life.
examples.zh: 他救了那个婴儿，但是却牺牲了自己的生命。

examples.en: The victory was won at the cost of many lives.
examples.zh: 胜利是用许多人的性命换来的。

costly.translation: a. 昂贵的, 奢华的, 费用大的

examples.en: Why did you get such a costly dictionary?
examples.zh: 为什么你买了一本那么贵的词典？

cottage.definition: n a small house with a single story

examples.en: There was a cottage on the side of the hill.
examples.zh: 山坡上有一个茅屋。

examples.en: He lives alone in a little cottage in the swamp.
examples.zh: 他独自一人住在沼泽地里的一栋小屋里。

examples.en: The old cottage has a certain charm about it.
examples.zh: 旧村屋有它自己一定的魅力。

cotton.definition:
n. soft silky fibers from cotton plants in their raw state
n. fabric woven from cotton fibers
n. erect bushy mallow plant or small tree bearing bolls containing seeds with many long hairy fibers
n. thread made of cotton fibers
cotton.translation: n. 棉花\nvi. 和谐, 有好感, 理解

examples.en: Their main exports are textiles, especially silk and cotton.
examples.zh: 他们主要输出的产品是纺织品，尤其以丝绸和绵为主。

examples.en: Someday I will buy a cotton candy machine.
examples.zh: 有一天我买了一台棉花糖机。

examples.en: Someday I'll buy a cotton candy machine.
examples.zh: 有一天我买了一台棉花糖机。

couch.definition: n. a flat coat of paint or varnish used by artists as a primer\nn. a narrow bed on which a patient lies during psychiatric or psychoanalytic treatment
couch.translation: n. 长沙发, 睡椅, 卧榻\nvt. 横躺, 表达\nvi. 躺下, 蹲伏

examples.en: Tom is in the living room, sleeping on the couch.
examples.zh: 汤姆在客厅长沙发上睡觉。

examples.en: A couch potato is something that I don't want to be.
examples.zh: 我不想成为整天泡在沙发上看电视的人。

examples.en: The TV remote control is under the couch.
examples.zh: 电视遥控器在沙发下面。

cough.definition: n. a sudden noisy expulsion of air from the lungs that clears the air passages; a common symptom of upper respiratory infection or bronchitis or pneumonia or tuberculosis\nv. exhale abruptly, as when one has a chest cold or congestion
cough.translation: n. 咳嗽\nvi. 咳嗽\nvt. 咳出

examples.en: Cover your mouth when you cough, sneeze, or yawn.
examples.zh: 你咳嗽、打喷嚏或打哈欠的时候要捂住你的嘴。

examples.en: I have a cough and a little fever.
examples.zh: 我咳嗽，还有点发烧。

examples.en: The cough syrup has a licorice flavoring.
examples.zh: 咳嗽糖浆有股甘草的味道。

could.definition:
imp. of Can
imp. Was, should be, or would be, able, capable, or
   susceptible. Used as an auxiliary, in the past tense or in the
   conditional present.

examples.en: If I were a bird, I could fly to you.
examples.zh: 如果我是一只小鸟，我就可以飞到你的身边了。

examples.en: I wish I could go to the party with you.
examples.zh: 我希望我能和你一起参加派对。

examples.en: Could you tell me where I can get a bus?
examples.zh: 你能告诉我能在哪里上公交车吗？

council.definition: n. a body serving in an administrative capacity\nn. (Christianity) an assembly of theologians and bishops and other representatives of different churches or dioceses that is convened to regulate matters of discipline or doctrine\nn. a meeting of people for consultation
council.translation: n. 会议, 委员会\n[经] 委员会

examples.en: You should run for city council.
examples.zh: 你应该去竞选城市委员会。

counsel.definition: n a lawyer who pleads cases in court\nn something that provides direction or advice as to a decision or course of action\nv give advice to
counsel.translation: n. 商议, 忠告, 法律顾问\nv. 商议, 劝告

examples.en: Give neither counsel nor salt until you are asked for.
He makes himself accessible to all who seek his counsel.
She made the decision by herself, without seeking my counsel.

count.definition:
n. the total number counted
n. the act of counting; reciting numbers in ascending order
n. a nobleman (in various countries) having rank equal to a British earl
v. determine the number or amount of
count.translation:
vt. 计算, 视为
vi. 计数
n. 计算, 合计, 计数, 伯爵
[计] 计数

examples.en: My son can count up to a hundred now.
examples.zh: 我儿子现在可以数到100。

examples.en: You could count to ten when you were two.
examples.zh: 在你两岁时, 你可以数到十。

examples.en: Tom closed his eyes and began to count sheep.
examples.zh: 汤姆闭上了眼睛开始数羊。

counter.definition:
n. table consisting of a horizontal surface over which business is transacted
n. game equipment (as a piece of wood, plastic, or ivory) used for keeping a count or reserving a space in various card or board games
n. a calculator that keeps a record of the number of times something happens
n. a person who counts things
counter.translation:
n. 计算器, 计算者, 柜台, 筹码
a. 反方向的, 相反的
adv. 反方向地, 相反地
[计] 计数器; 计数字

examples.en: He was sitting at the counter by himself.
examples.zh: 他独自坐在柜台旁。

examples.en: On which counter can I make my appointment?
examples.zh: 我可以在哪个柜台预约?

examples.en: Where is the United Airlines check-in counter?
examples.zh: 联合航空公司办理登机手续的柜台在哪里？

counterpart.definition: n. a person or thing having the same function or characteristics as another\nn. a duplicate copy
counterpart.translation: n. 副本, 复本, 配对物, 相应物\n[经] 副本, 正副二份中之一

examples.en: The Fuzhou Zoo in China's Fujian Province has done more than its counterparts in training pandas.
examples.zh: 中国福建省福州市动物园在训练大熊猫方面做得比它的同行多。

country.definition: n. the territory occupied by a nation\nn. an area outside of cities and towns
country.translation: n. 国家, 乡村, 地区, 故乡\na. 乡下的, 农村的\n[计] DOS外部命令:用于设定国家代码, 包括日期时间及货币格式

examples.en: How long do you plan to stay in this country?
examples.zh: 你打算在这个国家待多久？

examples.en: I love my country with every fiber of my being.
examples.zh: 我深爱我的祖国。

examples.en: The IMF ruled out any new loans to that country.
examples.zh: 国际货币基金组织不考虑再借款给该国。

countryside.translation: n. 乡下地方, 乡下居民

examples.en: My parents live a carefree life in the countryside.
examples.zh: 我父母在乡村过着无忧无虑的生活。

examples.en: A lot of trees grow in the countryside.
examples.zh: 乡间有很多树。

examples.en: There are lots of trees in the countryside.
examples.zh: 乡间有很多树。

county.definition: n. (United Kingdom) a region created by territorial division for the purpose of local government\nn. (United States) the largest administrative district within a state

examples.en: At Juancheng, Dong'e, and Fan counties, thanks to the strategic planning of Xun Yu and Cheng Yu, the locations were connected, and the cities were defended to the death.
examples.zh: 其鄄城、东阿、范县三处，赖荀彧、程昱二人设计相连，死守城郭。

couple.definition:
n. a pair who associate with one another
n. a pair of people who live together
n. a small indefinite number
n. two items of the same kind
couple.translation: n. 对, 夫妇, 数个\nvt. 使成双, 连接, 使成婚, 把...联系起来\nvi. 结合, 成婚

examples.en: I want to stay here for a couple of days.
examples.zh: 我想在这儿待几天。

examples.en: I'm going to stay here for a couple of days.
examples.zh: 我将要在这里待几天。

examples.en: You'll be all right again in a couple of days.
examples.zh: 你两三天就会回复健康了。

courage.definition: n. a quality of spirit that enables you to face danger or pain without showing fear

examples.en: I didn't have the courage to tell her the truth.
examples.zh: 我没有勇气把事实告诉她。

examples.en: Nobody had the courage to say it to him.
examples.zh: 没有人有勇气跟他说。

examples.en: I couldn't help but be impressed by Tom's courage.
examples.zh: 汤姆的勇气给我留下了深刻印象。

courageous.definition: a possessing or displaying courage; able to face and deal with danger or fear without flinching
courageous.translation: a. 勇敢的, 大胆的, 有胆量的

examples.en: Tom is very courageous, isn't he?
examples.zh: 汤姆非常勇敢，不是么？

examples.en: She's very courageous, isn't she?
examples.zh: 她很勇敢，不是吗？

examples.en: You are very courageous.
examples.zh: 您非常勇敢。

course.definition:
n. education imparted in a series of lessons or meetings
n. a connected series of events or actions or developments
n. general line of orientation
n. a mode of action
course.translation: n. 课程, 路线, 过程, 一道菜, 道路\nv. 追, (使)跑

examples.en: You can only let the matter take its own course.
examples.zh: 你只能听天由命。

examples.en: She has to take a remedial course in English.
examples.zh: 她需要上英语补习班。

examples.en: Of course, to die in Italy is more interesting.
examples.zh: 当然，死在义大利会更有意思。

court.definition:
n. an assembly (including one or more judges) to conduct judicial business
n. a room in which a lawcourt sits
n. the sovereign and his advisers who are the governing power of a state
n. a specially marked horizontal area within which a game is played
court.translation: n. 法院, 庭院, 奉承\nvt. 献殷勤, 追求, 招致\nvi. 求爱

examples.en: Anything you say can be used against you in court.
examples.zh: 你所说的一切都将成为呈堂证供。

examples.en: The accused is to appear before the court on Friday.
examples.zh: 被告周五将会出现在法庭上。

examples.en: The court declared him innocent on the charge of murder.
examples.zh: 法庭对他的谋杀罪名作出了无罪判决。

courtesy.definition: n. a courteous or respectful or considerate act\nn. a courteous or respectful or considerate remark\nn. a courteous manner
courtesy.translation: n. 礼貌, 谦恭, 好意\n[法] 优待, 礼貌, 恩惠

examples.en: "Exchanging courtesies every day is all we've done," Tom answered with resignation.
examples.zh: “天天寒暄就是我们做的所有事了。”汤姆无奈地回答。

cousin.definition: n. the child of your aunt or uncle
cousin.translation: n. 堂兄弟姊妹, 表兄弟姊妹\n[法] 同辈表亲或堂亲

examples.en: My cousin, who is a lawyer, is in France at present.
examples.zh: 我的律师表哥现在在法国。

examples.en: I get on very well with your cousin.
examples.zh: 我与你的表亲相处甚好。

examples.en: He went to stay with his cousin.
examples.zh: 他去和他的表弟待在一起了。

cover.definition:
n. the act of concealing the existence of something by obstructing the view of it
n. fire that makes it difficult for the enemy to fire on your own individuals or formations
n. a recording of a song that was first recorded or made popular by somebody else
n. a false identity and background (especially one created for an undercover agent)
cover.translation: n. 盖子, 封面, 藉口\nvt. 覆盖, 掩饰, 保护, 掩护, 包括\nvi. 覆盖

examples.en: What pain are you trying to cover up with alcohol?
examples.zh: 你借酒浇愁是为了什么事？

examples.en: Cover your head when you are in the sun.
examples.zh: 当你在阳光下的时候，遮住你的头。

examples.en: Cover your mouth when you cough, sneeze, or yawn.
examples.zh: 你咳嗽、打喷嚏或打哈欠的时候要捂住你的嘴。

coverage.definition: n. the total amount and type of insurance carried\nn. the extent to which something is covered\nn. the news as presented by reporters for newspapers or radio or television
coverage.translation: n. 覆盖的范围, 保险总额, 新闻报导\n[化] 可达范围; 覆盖度

examples.en: The channel has had to apologize for its biased coverage.
Your top does not provide enough midriff coverage, young lady.
The squadron encountered an ambush and scrambled for coverage.

cow.definition: n. female of domestic cattle: "`moo-cow' is a child's term"\nn. mature female of mammals of which the male is called `bull'\nn. a large unpleasant woman
cow.translation: n. 母牛, 母兽\nvt. 威胁

examples.en: In India, the cow is a sacred animal.
examples.zh: 在印度，牛是一种神圣的动物。

examples.en: The laser cow in WHAT THE CAR? is both hilarious and terrifying!
examples.zh: 《WHAT THE CAR?》中的雷射奶牛又好笑又吓人！

examples.en: There is a cow in the village.
examples.zh: 村里有一头母牛。

cozy.definition: s. enjoying or affording comforting warmth and shelter especially in a small space\ns. having or fostering a warm or friendly and informal atmosphere\ns. suggesting connivance
cozy.translation: a. 舒适的, 安逸的, 惬意的\nn. (茶壶等的)保暖罩, 舒适的座位\nvt. 以假话使安心

examples.en: His home is furnished in a very cozy way.
examples.zh: 他家的布局非常温馨。

examples.en: He lives in a cozy little house.
examples.zh: 他住在一个舒适的小房子里。

crack.definition:
n. a long narrow opening
n. a sudden sharp noise
n. a blemish resulting from a break without complete separation of the parts
n. a purified and potent form of cocaine that is smoked rather than snorted; highly addictive
crack.translation:
n. 裂缝, 爆裂声
v. (使)爆裂, (使)裂开, (使)发出爆裂声
a. 第一流的
adv. 啪地一声

examples.en: Tom tried to crack a walnut without damaging its kernel.
examples.zh: 汤姆试图敲碎一颗核桃而不损坏果仁。

examples.en: The chip in Yanni's windshield became a huge crack.
examples.zh: 雅尼的挡风玻璃上的碎片变成了一条巨大的裂缝。

examples.en: I can crack the password of this box.
examples.zh: 我能破译这个箱子的密码。

cradle.definition:
n. a baby bed with sides and rockers
n. birth of a person
v. hold gently and carefully
v. bring up from infancy
cradle.translation: n. 摇篮, 发祥地, 孩提时代\nvt. 放在摇篮内, 抚育\nvi. 刈割

examples.en: What is learned in the cradle is carried to the tomb.
examples.zh: 摇篮里学的带到坟墓。

examples.en: A baby is sleeping in the cradle.
examples.zh: 一个婴儿在摇篮里睡觉。

examples.en: The baby fell asleep in the cradle.
examples.zh: 宝宝在摇篮里入睡了。

craft.definition:
n. a vehicle designed for navigation in or on water or air or through outer space
n. people who perform a particular kind of skilled work
n. skill in an occupation or trade
n. shrewdness as demonstrated by being skilled in deception
craft.translation: n. 技艺, 手艺, 诡计\nvt. 精心制作

examples.en: "What craft do you know?" the wizard asked the youth.
examples.zh: 巫师问年轻人：「你懂什么技艺？」

examples.en: I greatly recommend reading it to anybody thinking of learning a craft.
examples.zh: 我强烈推荐任何想学习一门手艺的人都去读这本书。

examples.en: Sami had some arts and crafts things to do.
examples.zh: 萨米有一些手工艺术方面的事情要做。

crash.definition:
n. a serious accident (usually involving one or more vehicles)
n. a sudden large decline of business or the prices of stocks (especially one that causes additional failures)
n. the act of colliding with something
n. (computer science) an event that causes a computer system to become inoperative
crash.translation:
n. 哗啦声, 猛撞, 崩溃, 粗布
v. 撞碎, 破碎, (使)...坠毁
a. 速成的
[计] 崩溃

examples.en: She won't take an airplane for fear of a crash.
examples.zh: 她不会乘飞机因为害怕坠机。

examples.en: Ten years ago, our parents died in a car crash.
examples.zh: 十年前，我们的父母死于一场车祸。

examples.en: Tom died two years ago in a plane crash.
examples.zh: 汤姆死于两年前的一次空难。

crawl.definition:
n. a very slow movement
n. a swimming stroke; arms are moved alternately overhead accompanied by a flutter kick
n. a slow mode of locomotion on hands and knees or dragging the body
v. move slowly; in the case of people or animals with the body near the ground
crawl.translation: n. 爬行, 匍匐而行, 养鱼池\nv. 爬行

examples.en: I'm so embarrassed I could dig a hole and crawl into it.
examples.zh: 我窘得想找个洞钻进去。

examples.en: She knows how to do the crawl.
examples.zh: 她知道怎么游自由式。

examples.en: The area around the melting ice cream was crawling with ants.
examples.zh: 在那滩冰淇淋的周围，有一群蚂蚁在爬来爬去。

crazy.definition:
n. someone deranged and possibly dangerous
s. foolish; totally unsound
s. possessed by inordinate excitement
s. bizarre or fantastic
crazy.translation: a. 发狂的, 狂热的

examples.en: Grr! I'm itchy all over, and it's driving me crazy.
examples.zh: 哎呦好难受啊，全身发痒！

examples.en: How did you come up with this crazy idea?
examples.zh: 你是怎么想到这么疯狂的主意的？

examples.en: He is not just interested, he's crazy about it.
examples.zh: 他不仅是对这个有兴趣，并相当热衷。

cream.definition:
n. the best people or things in a group
n. the part of milk containing the butterfat
n. toiletry consisting of any of various substances in the form of a thick liquid that have a soothing and moisturizing effect when applied to the skin
v. make creamy by beating
cream.translation: n. 乳酪, 奶油, 面霜\n[医] 乳油, 乳皮; 乳膏, 霜

examples.en: If you buy me an ice cream, I'll kiss you.
examples.zh: 如果你买给我冰淇淋，我就亲你一下。

examples.en: The heat is making me crave for an ice cream.
examples.zh: 热得想吃冰淇淋。

examples.en: Eating ice cream always puts me in a happy mood.
examples.zh: 我一吃冰淇淋就高兴。

create.definition:
v. bring into existence
v. pursue a creative activity; be engaged in a creative activity
v. invest with a new title, office, or rank
v. create by artistic means
create.translation: vt. 创造, 建造, 引起, 任命

examples.en: Mathematics is the language that God used to create the universe.
examples.zh: 数学是上帝用来创造宇宙的语言。

examples.en: Karlo has the ability to understand and create.
examples.zh: Karlo有理解和创造的能力。

examples.en: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
examples.zh: 起初，神创造了天地。

creation.definition:
n. the human act of creating
n. an artifact that has been brought into existence by someone
n. the event that occurred at the beginning of something
n. (theology) God's act of bringing the universe into existence
creation.translation: n. 创造, 创作物, 发明\n[化] 产生

examples.en: Love is what gives joy to all creation.
examples.zh: 爱把喜悦带给所有的生命。

creative.definition: a. having the ability or power to create\ns. promoting construction or creation
creative.translation: a. 有创造力的, 创作的, 产生的

examples.en: Tom has a lot of creative ideas.
examples.zh: 汤姆有很多有创意的主意。

examples.en: I don't know how long I'll have to wait before I become more creative.
examples.zh: 不知道要等多长时间，我的创作能力才能进步。

examples.en: I don't know how long I'll have to wait before my creative ability improves.
examples.zh: 不知道要等多长时间，我的创作能力才能进步。

creature.definition: n. a human being; `wight' is an archaic term\nn. a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
creature.translation: n. 人, 动物, 创造物, 生物

examples.en: Lucario is a creature in the Pokémon series.
examples.zh: 路卡利欧是《神奇宝贝》系列中的一种生物。

examples.en: How can there exist a creature as adorable as a cat?
examples.zh: 怎么会有猫咪这么可爱的生物？

examples.en: Tom says that he's a creature of habit.
examples.zh: 汤姆说他是习惯的产物。

credit.definition:
n. money available for a client to borrow
n. an accounting entry acknowledging income or capital items
n. used in the phrase `to your credit' in order to indicate an achievement deserving praise; 
n. arrangement for deferred payment for goods and services
credit.translation: n. 信用, 信任, 荣誉, 贷款, 学分\nvt. 归功于, 赞颂, 信任, 相信\n[计] 信用量

examples.en: Did you bring cash or your credit card with you?
examples.zh: 你钱或者信用卡带来没有？

examples.en: I would like to pay with a credit card.
examples.zh: 我想用信用卡付款。

examples.en: I usually use a credit card instead of cash.
examples.zh: 我经常用信用卡，而不是钞票。

crew.definition: n. the men and women who man a vehicle (ship, aircraft, etc.)\nn. the team of men manning a racing shell\nv. serve as a crew member on
crew.translation: n. 全体人员, 一群人, 全体队员\ncrow的过去式

examples.en: Modern ships only need a small crew.
examples.zh: 现代船只只需要一小组的船员。

examples.en: Captains have responsibility for ship and crew.
examples.zh: 船长们对他们的船只和船员负有责任。

examples.en: Some of the crew were drowned.
examples.zh: 有几个船员溺水而亡。

crime.definition: n. (criminal law) an act punishable by law; usually considered an evil act\nn. an evil act not necessarily punishable by law
crime.translation: n. 犯罪, 罪行, 罪恶\n[法] 犯罪, 罪, 罪恶

examples.en: And if I were gay, would that be a crime?
examples.zh: 如果我是同志那又怎样？这能构成犯罪吗？

examples.en: I am not connected to this crime in any way.
examples.zh: 我与这起犯罪没有任何关系。

examples.en: He ought to be punished if he commits a crime.
examples.zh: 如果他犯了罪，他应该受到惩罚。

criminal.definition: n. someone who has committed a crime or has been legally convicted of a crime\ns. guilty of crime or serious offense\ns. involving or being or having the nature of a crime
criminal.translation: n. 罪犯, 犯人, 刑事\na. 犯了罪的, 刑事的, 有罪的

examples.en: The criminal came out of the house with arms raised.
examples.zh: 犯人手举在空中走出了房子。

examples.en: That is a criminal offense, and you will surely be punished!
examples.zh: 那是犯罪行为，你肯定会受到惩罚的!

examples.en: The police were able to find the criminal.
examples.zh: 警方能够找到罪犯。

crisis.definition: n. an unstable situation of extreme danger or difficulty\nn. a crucial stage or turning point in the course of something
crisis.translation: n. 危机, 危险期, 紧要关头\n[医] 危象; 骤退, 临界, 极期

examples.en: That documentary about the environmental crisis was a real eye-opener.
examples.zh: 这部有关环境危机的纪录片真是令人大开眼界。

examples.en: Algeria is in the midst of a political crisis.
examples.zh: 阿尔及利亚正处于政治危机中。

examples.en: Algeria is in the midst of an economic crisis.
examples.zh: 阿尔及利亚正处于经济危机中。

criterion.definition: n. the ideal in terms of which something can be judged
criterion.translation: n. 标准, 准则, 规范\n[化] 判据

examples.en: The criterion of the scientific status of a theory is its falsifiability, or refutability, or testability.
examples.zh: 一个理论的科学地位的标准是它的可证伪性、可反驳性或可检验性。

examples.en: Americans are said to regard the amount of money a man makes as a criterion of his ability.
examples.zh: 据说美国人把一个人的收入视为评判他能力的重要尺度。

critic.definition: n. a person who is professionally engaged in the analysis and interpretation of works of art\nn. anyone who expresses a reasoned judgment of something\nn. someone who frequently finds fault or makes harsh and unfair judgments
critic.translation: n. 批评家, 鉴定家

examples.en: This famous mountain climber is a critic of mass tourism.
examples.zh: 这位著名的登山家批评大众旅游。

examples.en: Critics are coming down hard on tightened economic restrictions.
examples.zh: 对严格限制经济的批评蜂拥而来。

critical.definition:
a. marked by a tendency to find and call attention to errors and flaws
a. at or of a point at which a property or phenomenon suffers an abrupt change especially having enough mass to sustain a chain reaction
a. characterized by careful evaluation and judgment
s. urgently needed; absolutely necessary
critical.translation: a. 批评的, 决定性的, 危险的, 临界的\n[医] 危象的; 临界的, 极期的

examples.en: I can't understand why you are so critical of him.
examples.zh: 我不明白为什么你这么批评他。

examples.en: Your mother is in critical condition.
examples.zh: 你母亲现在情况危殆。

examples.en: The situation there was critical.
examples.zh: 那里的情况很危急。

criticism.definition: n. disapproval expressed by pointing out faults or shortcomings\nn. a serious examination and judgment of something\nn. a written evaluation of a work of literature
criticism.translation: n. 批评, 评论, 非难\n[法] 批判, 批评, 评论

examples.en: The more public the work, the more criticism you receive.
examples.zh: 工作越公开，批评就越多。

examples.en: The purpose of criticism is to construct, not to destroy.
examples.zh: 批评的目的是建设而不是破坏。

examples.en: Tom found Mary's constant criticism of him hard to cope with.
examples.zh: 汤姆认为和经常批评他的玛丽很难相处。

criticize.translation: v. 批评, 吹毛求疵, 非难

examples.en: I don't mind being criticized when I am wrong.
examples.zh: 要是我说错话被人议论，我是不管的。

examples.en: Few, if any, will criticize him.
examples.zh: 很少有人会批评他，即使有也不多。

examples.en: England’s goalkeeper was criticized for the amount of goals he conceded.
examples.zh: 英格兰的守门员因为自己失球过多而被批评。

crop.definition:
n. the yield from plants in a single growing season
n. a cultivated plant that is grown commercially on a large scale
n. a collection of people or things appearing together
n. the output of something in a season
crop.translation:
n. 农作物, 产量, 平头
vt. 收割, 修剪, 种植
vi. 收获
[计] 裁剪

examples.en: Without bee pollination, California's almond crop, for example, would be non-existent.
examples.zh: 例如，如果没有蜜蜂授粉，加州的杏仁作物就不会存在。

examples.en: Through genetic modification, we can improve crops.
examples.zh: 通过遗传修饰，我们可以改良农作物。

examples.en: The farmer warned the children not to stomp on the freshly planted crops.
examples.zh: 农夫警告孩子们不要践踏新栽种的作物。

cross.definition:
n. a wooden structure consisting of an upright post with a transverse piece
n. a representation of the structure on which Jesus was crucified; used as an emblem of Christianity or in heraldry
n. any affliction that causes great suffering
v. fold so as to resemble a cross
cross.translation:
n. 十字架, 十字架形物件, 交叉, 十字标, 交叉路, 磨难, 杂交
a. 生气的, 交叉的, 相反的
v. 交叉, 横过, 越过
[计] 交叉, 十字标

examples.en: It is very pleasant to cross the ocean by ship.
examples.zh: 乘船过海非常舒服。

examples.en: The Red Cross constantly supplies food to the disaster areas.
examples.zh: 红十字会不断地给灾区提供食物援助。

examples.en: Look out for cars when you cross the road.
examples.zh: 当你过马路的时候要当心汽车。

crowd.definition:
n. a large number of things or people considered together
n. an informal body of friends
v. fill or occupy to the point of overflowing
v. to gather together in large numbers
crowd.translation: n. 群众, 一伙人\nvt. 拥挤, 挤满, 挤进

examples.en: We lost sight of the man in the crowd.
examples.zh: 在人群中，我们失去了那个男人的踪影。

examples.en: A crowd of people gathered to see the parade.
examples.zh: 一大群人聚在一起看巡游。

examples.en: The crowd obstructed the police in the discharge of their duties.
examples.zh: 群众妨碍了警员执行任务。

crucial.definition: a. of extreme importance; vital to the resolution of a crisis\ns. having crucial relevance
crucial.translation: a. 决定性的, 重要的, 严厉的\n[医] 十字形的; 决断的, 定局的

examples.en: The next four to six weeks are crucial in controlling the massive Ebola outbreak.
examples.zh: 接下来的四到六周将对于控制伊波拉病毒的大爆发至关重要。

examples.en: This is a crucial point.
examples.zh: 这是一个关键点。

crude.definition:
s. not carefully or expertly made
s. conspicuously and tastelessly indecent
s. belonging to an early stage of technical development; characterized by simplicity and (often) crudeness
s. not processed or subjected to analysis
crude.translation: a. 天然的, 未成熟的, 粗糙的, 粗鲁的\nn. 天然的物质

examples.en: Don't tell crude jokes in the presence of my father.
Tom said something crude about the way Mary was dressed.
A tanker is a ship that carries crude oil.

cruel.definition: s (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
cruel.translation: a. 残酷的, 令人极痛苦的\n[法] 残忍的, 残酷的

examples.en: It is cruel of him to say such things to her.
examples.zh: 他跟她说这样的话真是太残忍了。

examples.en: The poor people were at the mercy of the cruel dictator.
examples.zh: 可怜的人民任凭残暴的独裁者处置。

examples.en: I never thought he was capable of doing something so cruel.
examples.zh: 我从来没想到他能做到那么残忍的事。

cruise.definition:
n. an ocean trip taken for pleasure
v. drive around aimlessly but ostentatiously and at leisure
v. travel at a moderate speed
v. look for a sexual partner in a public place
cruise.translation: n. 巡航, 巡弋, 漫游\nv. 巡航, 巡弋, 漫游

examples.en: The straits were too narrow for the cruise ship.
examples.zh: 这个海峡对游艇来说太窄了。

crush.definition:
n. a dense crowd of people
n. the act of crushing
v. break into small pieces
v. humiliate or depress completely
crush.translation: n. 压碎, 粉碎, 群众, 迷恋\nvt. 压破, 征服, 塞, 弄皱, 榨出\nvi. 被压碎, 起皱, 挤

examples.en: She has a crush on the boy next door.
examples.zh: 她看上了隔壁的那个男孩。

examples.en: I think that Tom has a crush on Mary.
examples.zh: 我觉得汤姆爱上玛丽了。

examples.en: It looks like Tom has a crush on Mary.
examples.zh: 看来汤姆热恋着玛丽。

cry.definition:
n. a loud utterance; often in protest or opposition
n. a loud utterance of emotion (especially when inarticulate)
n. a fit of weeping
n. the characteristic utterance of an animal
cry.translation: n. 叫声, 哭声, 大叫\nvi. 哭, 叫, 喊\nvt. 叫喊, 大声说, 哭出

examples.en: She began to cry at the sight of my face.
examples.zh: 她看到我的脸就开始哭。

examples.en: I'm under so much pressure, I just want to cry.
examples.zh: 我压力好大，我真想哭。

examples.en: I don't know if I should cry or laugh.
examples.zh: 我不知道我该哭还是该笑。

crystal.definition:
n. a solid formed by the solidification of a chemical and having a highly regular atomic structure
n. a crystalline element used as a component in various electronic devices
n. a rock formed by the solidification of a substance; has regularly repeating internal structure; external plane faces
n. glassware made of quartz
crystal.translation: n. 水晶, 水晶装饰品, 结晶\na. 水晶的, 水晶一样的, 透明的

examples.en: I found a beautiful crystal on the beach last year.
Sami was talking about some sort of a healing crystal.
"That makes it as clear as crystal," said the inspector.

cube.definition:
n. a hexahedron with six equal squares as faces
n. the product of three equal terms
n. any of several tropical American woody plants of the genus Lonchocarpus whose roots are used locally as a fish poison and commercially as a source of rotenone
n. a block in the (approximate) shape of a cube
cube.translation: n. 立方体, 立方\n[机] 立方体, 立方

examples.en: When the heater in the barn fails, you get milk-flavoured ice cubes.
examples.zh: 当牛舍的暖气坏了, 你就会有牛奶味的冰块。

examples.en: This is an ice cube.
examples.zh: 这是冰块。

examples.en: Three cubed is twenty-seven.
examples.zh: 三的立方是二十七。

cultivate.definition: v. foster the growth of\nv. prepare for crops

examples.en: Good habits should be cultivated in childhood.
examples.zh: 好习惯是从小养成的。

cultural.definition:
a. of or relating to the arts and manners that a group favors
s. denoting or deriving from or distinctive of the ways of living built up by a group of people
a. of or relating to the shared knowledge and values of a society
a. relating to the raising of plants or animals
cultural.translation: a. 文化的, 教养的, 修养的\n[医] 培养的

examples.en: The dragon is one of the cultural emblems of China.
examples.zh: 龙是中国的文化图腾。

examples.en: Furthermore, I still don't think this a huge cultural difference.
examples.zh: 而且，我还是认为这准不是个巨大的文化区别。

examples.en: Cultural exchange programs can strengthen friendly relations between neighboring countries.
examples.zh: 文化交流计划可以加强邻国之间的友好关系。

culture.definition:
n. a particular society at a particular time and place
n. the tastes in art and manners that are favored by a social group
n. (biology) the growing of microorganisms in a nutrient medium (such as gelatin or agar)
n. the attitudes and behavior that are characteristic of a particular social group or organization
culture.translation: n. 文化, 修养, 耕种\nvt. 耕种, 培养

examples.en: In culture, they are on the same plane as savages.
examples.zh: 在教养上，他们可以说是和野蛮人差不多。

examples.en: We should pass on our culture to the next generation.
examples.zh: 我们应当把文化传承到下一代。

examples.en: The manners and customs of a country reflect its culture.
examples.zh: 一个国家的风俗习惯反映了它的文化。

cunning.definition: n. crafty artfulness (especially in deception)\ns. attractive especially by means of smallness or prettiness or quaintness
cunning.translation: a. 狡猾的, 巧妙的, 可爱的\n[法] 狡猾的的, 狡诈的, 熟练的

examples.en: People say that the fox is more cunning than other animals.
examples.zh: 人们说，狐狸比其他动物要狡猾。

cup.definition:
n. a small open container usually used for drinking; usually has a handle
n. the quantity a cup will hold
n. any cup-shaped concavity
n. a United States liquid unit equal to 8 fluid ounces
cup.translation: n. 杯子, 茶杯, 优胜杯\nvt. 使成杯状, 为...拔火罐

examples.en: I had a cup of coffee at the coffee shop.
examples.zh: 我在咖啡店里喝了一杯咖啡。

examples.en: The World Cup is going to start on the 11th.
examples.zh: 世界杯 11 号就要开始了。

examples.en: We were waiting for him over a cup of coffee.
examples.zh: 我们边喝咖啡边等他。

cupboard.definition: n. a small room (or recess) or cabinet used for storage space
cupboard.translation: n. 食橱, 碗柜, 餐具柜

examples.en: Tom opened the shoe cupboard and took the shoes out.
examples.zh: 汤姆打开鞋柜拿出鞋。

examples.en: Open the cupboard to the left, the bottles are in there.
examples.zh: 打开左边的橱，瓶子在那儿。

examples.en: She folded up the towels and put them away in the cupboard.
examples.zh: 她把毛巾折叠好再放入柜子里。

cure.definition: v. prepare by drying, salting, or chemical processing in order to preserve\nv. make (substances) hard and improve their usability\nv. be or become preserved
cure.translation: n. 治疗, 治愈, 治疗法\nvt. 治疗, 治愈, 改正, 腌制, 加工处理, 使硫化\nvi. 受治疗, 被加工处理, 被硫化

examples.en: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.
examples.zh: 预防胜于治疗。

examples.en: Scientists have not found a method yet to cure cancer.
examples.zh: 科学家们还没有找到癌症的治疗方法。

examples.en: This medicine will cure you of your skin disease.
examples.zh: 这药可以治疗你的皮肤病。

curiosity.definition: n. a state in which you want to learn more about something
curiosity.translation: n. 好奇心, 新奇的事物, 珍品

examples.en: Today's Beijing has given me a very deep impression and aroused my curiosity.
examples.zh: 现代的北京给了我深刻的印象，也激起了我的好奇心。

examples.en: Curiosity killed the cat.
examples.zh: 好奇会吃苦头的。

curious.definition: s. beyond or deviating from the usual or expected\na. eager to investigate and learn or learn more (sometimes about others' concerns)\ns. having curiosity aroused; eagerly interested in learning more
curious.translation: a. 好奇的, 求知的, 古怪的

examples.en: She was so curious that she opened the box.
examples.zh: 她太过好奇，以至于打开了盒子。

examples.en: She is curious to find who sent the flowers.
examples.zh: 她很想知道那束花是谁寄来的。

examples.en: She's curious to find out who sent the flowers.
examples.zh: 她很想知道那束花是谁寄来的。

currency.definition: n. the metal or paper medium of exchange that is presently used\nn. general acceptance or use
currency.translation: n. 货币, 通货, 流通, 通用\n[计] 货币, 货币型

examples.en: The exchange rates for foreign currency change daily.
examples.zh: 外币的汇率天天都变。

examples.en: What currency do you use in England?
examples.zh: 你在英国用什么钱买东西？

examples.en: What is the currency of Taiwan?
examples.zh: 台湾的货币是什么 ?

current.definition: n. a flow of electricity through a conductor\nn. a steady flow of a fluid (usually from natural causes)\na. occurring in or belonging to the present time
current.translation: n. 涌流, 趋势, 流\na. 流通的, 现在的, 当前的, 流行的\n[计] 当前的

examples.en: The article begins with an account of the current situation.
examples.zh: 文章开头讲了当前的形势。

examples.en: Judging from the current situation, this project is sure to succeed.
examples.zh: 根据当前的状况，这个项目绝对会成功。

examples.en: We rowed up the river against the current.
examples.zh: 我们在河里划著船逆流而上。

currently.definition: r at this time or period; now
currently.translation: adv. 现在, 当前, 一般, 普通\n[计] 当前

examples.en: Currently there are still women who like to wear corsets.
examples.zh: 现在仍然有女生喜欢穿束腹。

examples.en: Currently, my sister works as a cashier at a supermarket.
examples.zh: 目前，我妹妹在一家超市当收银员。

examples.en: Currently, having a hood is part of young people's fashion.
examples.zh: 现代年轻人戴风帽是装一种派头。

curriculum.definition: n an integrated course of academic studies
curriculum.translation: n. 课程\n[医] 课程, 学程

examples.en: I have attached a PDF file of my curriculum vitae.
Some state laws leave curriculum decisions to individual school districts.
The curriculum of this school is wide and shallow.

curse.definition:
n. profane or obscene expression usually of surprise or anger
n. a severe affliction
v. utter obscenities or profanities
v. heap obscenities upon
curse.translation: n. 咒骂, 诅咒\nvt. 诅咒, 咒骂

examples.en: Yes, people usually curse at someone they are acquainted with.
examples.zh: 对，人通常会对自己的熟人口出恶言。

curtain.definition: n. hanging cloth used as a blind (especially for a window)\nn. any barrier to communication or vision\nv. provide with drapery
curtain.translation: n. 帐, 幕, 窗帘\nvt. 装帘子于, 遮蔽

examples.en: A green carpet will not go with this blue curtain.
examples.zh: 绿色的毯子和这条蓝色的帘子不配。

examples.en: She hung a curtain over the window.
examples.zh: 她把窗帘挂在窗户上。

examples.en: He came out from behind the curtain.
examples.zh: 他从窗帘后出来了。

curve.definition: n. the trace of a point whose direction of motion changes\nn. a line on a graph representing data\nn. a pitch of a baseball that is thrown with spin so that its path curves as it approaches the batter
curve.translation: n. 曲线, 弯曲, 曲线球\nvt. 弯, 使弯曲\nvi. 成曲形

examples.en: In its graphical representation, the normal distribution is a bell-shaped curve, with the value growing as one moves closer to the middle and decreasing as one moves away.
examples.zh: 在图形上，正态分布是一种钟形曲线，越接近中心，取值越大，越远离中心，取值越小。

cushion.definition: n. the layer of air that supports a hovercraft or similar vehicle\nn. a soft bag filled with air or a mass of padding such as feathers or foam rubber etc.\nv. protect from impact
cushion.translation: n. 垫子, 橡皮软垫\nvt. 加垫褥, 缓冲, 掩盖

examples.en: The benches are hard, so I always bring a cushion.
Ziri collapsed on the couch and cried into the cushion.
Don't use the radio as a pillow or cushion.

custody.translation: n. 监护, 拘留, 监禁\n[经] 保管, 照顾, 保护

examples.en: As for the papers, I have custody of them.
examples.zh: 至于该文件，我在保管。

examples.en: The man was held in police custody.
examples.zh: 这个男人被警察拘留了。

examples.en: The police held him in custody.
examples.zh: 警方拘留了他。

custom.definition: n. accepted or habitual practice\nn. a specific practice of long standing\nn. habitual patronage
custom.translation: n. 习惯, 风俗, 海关, 自定义\na. 定制的\n[计] 定制; 自定义

examples.en: It's my custom to go for a walk before breakfast.
examples.zh: 我习惯早餐之前出去散步。

examples.en: As was the custom in those days, he married young.
examples.zh: 如当时的习惯，他很年轻便成婚了。

examples.en: According to custom, the bride should be compliant.
examples.zh: 根据习俗，新娘应该循规蹈矩。

customer.definition: n. someone who pays for goods or services
customer.translation: n. 消费者\n[化] 顾客

examples.en: It is a fact that I'm poor at customer service.
examples.zh: 事实上，我的客服能力很差。

examples.en: I want to ensure my phone has good customer support.
examples.zh: 我想要确定手机能有优秀的客户服务。

examples.en: Employees of the call centre answer all customer service calls.
examples.zh: 呼叫中心的员工负责接听所有客服电话。

customs.definition: n. money collected under a tariff\nn. money collected under a tariff
customs.translation: n. 海关, 关卡, 关税\n[经] 关税, 海关

examples.en: I was searched by the customs officers at the airport.
examples.zh: 我在机场被海关人员搜查。

examples.en: The manners and customs of a country reflect its culture.
examples.zh: 一个国家的风俗习惯反映了它的文化。

examples.en: These old customs have been handed down from generation to generation.
examples.zh: 这些古老习俗都是一代一代相传下来的。

cut.definition:
n. a share of the profits
n. (film) an immediate transition from one shot to the next
n. a trench resembling a furrow that was made by erosion or excavation
n. a step on some scale
cut.translation:
n. 切口, 割伤, 降低, 切, 割, 砍, 削, 伤口, 削减, 缩短, 删节, 通路
a. 经切割的, 缩减的
vt. 切, 割, 减少, 刺痛, 开辟, 雕刻, 删节, 缩短, 停止, 排斥, 切断, 关, 显出
vi. 切, 割, 砍, 刺痛, 相交, 抄近路, 剪辑
[计] 剪切

examples.en: Do you know the reason why he cut class today?
examples.zh: 你知道为什么他今天逃课了吗？

examples.en: I had my hair cut at the barber shop yesterday.
examples.zh: 我昨天去了理发店理发。

examples.en: The doctor advised my father to cut down on smoking.
examples.zh: 医生建议我父亲少吸烟。

cycle.definition:
n. an interval during which a recurring sequence of events occurs
n. a series of poems or songs on the same theme
n. a periodically repeated sequence of events
n. a single complete execution of a periodically repeated phenomenon
cycle.translation:
n. 周期, 循环, 自行车, 一段时间, 整套
vi. 循环, 轮转, 骑自行车
vt. 使循环, 使轮转
[计] 环路; 周期; 循环

examples.en: Usually I cycle or get the bus to work.
examples.zh: 我通常骑自行车或乘公交车去上班。

examples.en: Most of the pupils here cycle to school.
examples.zh: 这儿的学生大多骑车上学。

examples.en: You may go cycling if it doesn't rain.
examples.zh: 如果不下雨的话，你可以去踏单车。

cylinder.definition:
n. a solid bounded by a cylindrical surface and two parallel planes (the bases)
n. a surface generated by rotating a parallel line around a fixed line
n. a chamber within which piston moves
n. a cylindrical container for oxygen or compressed air
cylinder.translation: n. 圆筒, 圆筒状物, 汽缸, 柱面\n[计] 柱面

examples.en: The piston does not come into contact with the cylinder cover.
examples.zh: 这个活塞不接触汽缸盖。

calamity.definition: n. an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
calamity.translation: n. 灾难, 不幸事件

examples.en: Why did you bring calamity to us in this way?
I did not escape any calamity. Mash potatoes!
I have not escaped any calamity. Mash potatoes!

calcium.definition: n. a white metallic element that burns with a brilliant light; the fifth most abundant element in the earth's crust; an important component of most plants and animals

examples.en: Calcium, heated with a Bunsen burner, turns the flame orange-red.
Spinach is a rich source of iron and calcium.
Calcium is a chemical element with the symbol Ca.

caliber.definition: n a degree or grade of excellence or worth\nn diameter of a tube or gun barrel
caliber.translation: n. 口径, 才干, 水准\n[医] 管径, 口径

examples.en: That is a high caliber rifle.
I'm nowhere near her caliber.
I know a bit about calligraphy.
examples.zh: 我对书法略知一二。

examples.en: Are you good at calligraphy?
examples.zh: 你擅长书法吗？

camouflage.definition: n. fabric dyed with splotches of green and brown and black and tan; intended to make the wearer of a garment made of this fabric hard to distinguish from the background\nn. device or stratagem for concealment or deceit\nv. disguise by camouflaging; exploit the natural surroundings to disguise something
camouflage.translation: vt. 伪装, 掩饰\nn. 伪装, 伪装物, 幌子

examples.en: Ziri noticed a deer stand with a camouflage netting around it.
The expected direction was confused by the dazzling camouflage
Most of the soldiers were wearing camouflage uniforms.

canopy.definition:
n. the transparent covering of an aircraft cockpit
n. the umbrellalike part of a parachute that fills with air
n. a covering (usually of cloth) that serves as a roof to shelter an area from the weather
v. cover with a canopy
canopy.translation: n. 天篷, 遮篷, 苍穹\nvt. 用天蓬遮盖

examples.en: Inna lay down under the canopy and fell fast asleep.
The tree's canopy was a natural umbrella in the rain.
The first beams of sunlight came glistening through the canopy.

cape.definition: n. a strip of land projecting into a body of water\nn. a sleeveless garment like a cloak but shorter
cape.translation: n. 岬, 海角, 披肩, 斗蓬

examples.en: The languages spoken in Cape Verde are Portuguese and creoles.
In 1434, Portuguese navigator and explorer Gil Eanes rounded Cape Bojador.
My dream is to study Afrikaans in Cape Town.

capitalist.definition: n. a conservative advocate of capitalism\nn. a person who invests capital in a business (especially a large business)\na. of or relating to capitalism or capitalists
capitalist.translation: n. 资本家, 资本主义者\na. 资本主义的

examples.en: God knows how many Valentine's Days capitalists have invented.
examples.zh: 天知道资本家创造了多少个情人节。

examples.en: The capitalists tend to exploit the working people.
examples.zh: 资本家倾向于压榨工人。

examples.en: China is a capitalist country.
examples.zh: 中国是资本主义国家。

capsule.definition:
n. a small container
n. a pill in the form of a small rounded gelatinous container with medicine inside
n. a dry dehiscent seed vessel or the spore-containing structure of e.g. mosses
n. a structure that encloses a body part
capsule.translation: n. 胶囊, 蒴果, 瓶帽, 航天舱\n[化] 胶囊剂

examples.en: This building is a capsule hotel lodging men and women.
examples.zh: 那个建筑物是男女都可以住宿的胶囊酒店。

caption.definition: n. taking exception; especially a quibble based on a captious argument\nn. brief description accompanying an illustration\nv. provide with a caption, as of a photograph or a drawing
caption.translation: n. 说明, 字幕, 标题\nvt. 加上标题, 加上说明\n[计] 标题

examples.en: Some signs have a symbol and a separate caption.
Generate a concise and descriptive caption for this image.
Fewer graphics and more captions would make the description clearer.

captive.definition:
n. an animal that is confined
n. a person held in the grip of a strong emotion or passion
s. being in captivity
s. giving or marked by complete attention to
captive.translation: n. 俘虏, 迷恋者\na. 被俘的, 被迷住的

examples.en: Tom is being held captive.
examples.zh: 汤姆被囚禁了。

cardinal.definition:
n. (Roman Catholic Church) one of a group of more than 100 prominent bishops in the Sacred College who advise the Pope and elect new Popes
n. a variable color averaging a vivid red
n. crested thick-billed North American finch having bright red plumage in the male
s. serving as an essential component
cardinal.translation: n. 红衣主教, 鲜红色\na. 主要的, 深红色的

examples.en: One is a cardinal number; first is an ordinal number.
"What kind of bird is that?" "Looks like a cardinal."
There are four cardinal points: East, south, west and north.

caretaker.definition: n. a custodian who is hired to take care of something (property or a person)\nn. an official who performs the duties of an office temporarily
caretaker.translation: n. 照顾者, 看管者, 看守人\n[法] 看守员, 管理员, 看管人

examples.en: The accident was due to the negligence of the caretaker.
The animal caretaker is giving the dogs their feed.
He has been the caretaker of this house for forty years.

carnival.definition: n. a festival marked by merrymaking and processions\nn. a traveling show; having sideshows and rides and games of skill etc.
carnival.translation: n. 嘉年华会, 狂欢节, 饮宴狂欢

examples.en: Not all Brazilians enjoy Carnival.
examples.zh: 不是所有巴西人都喜欢狂欢节。

carp.definition: n. the lean flesh of a fish that is often farmed; can be baked or braised\nn. any of various freshwater fish of the family Cyprinidae
carp.translation: n. 鲤鱼\nvi. 吹毛求疵, 挑剔

examples.en: Fish such as carp and trout live in fresh water.
examples.zh: 鲤鱼和鳟鱼等鱼类生活在淡水中。

cartridge.definition: n. ammunition consisting of a cylindrical casing containing an explosive charge and a bullet; fired from a rifle or handgun\nn. a module designed to be inserted into a larger piece of equipment\nn. an electro-acoustic transducer that is the part of the arm of a record player that holds the needle and that is removable
cartridge.translation: n. 弹药筒, 弹药, 一卷软片, 墨粉鼓\n[计] 盒式磁带机

examples.en: Please replace the empty ink cartridge in the printer.
examples.zh: 请把打印机里面的空的墨粉鼓换掉。

cascade.definition:
n. a small waterfall or series of small waterfalls
n. a succession of stages or operations or processes or units
v. rush down in big quantities, like a cascade
v. arrange (open windows) on a computer desktop so that they overlap each other, with the title bars visible
cascade.translation: n. 小瀑布, 瀑布状物\nvi. 成瀑布落下\n[计] 层叠, 级联

examples.en: As this is a cascade with multiple layers, it shouldn't be surprising that it's slow.
examples.zh: 因为这是一个有好几层的瀑布，所以速度慢也不会让人惊讶。

catastrophe.definition: n. a state of extreme (usually irremediable) ruin and misfortune\nn. a sudden violent change in the earth's surface
catastrophe.translation: n. 大灾难, 大祸\n[化] 突变

examples.en: Due to the catastrophe caused by the huge tsunami, damage was sustained by the nuclear reactor as well as explosions at the nuclear power plant.
examples.zh: 由于特大海啸的灾害，核能融炉遭受损害，造成了原子能发电站爆炸。

categorical.definition: a. relating to or included in a category or categories
categorical.translation: a. 范畴的, 绝对的, 明确的

examples.en: I don't want to be too categorical!

cavalry.definition: n. troops trained to fight on horseback\nn. a highly mobile army unit

examples.en: The enemy cavalry crossed the river by an unknown ford.
The cavalry galloped to the capital to report their victory.
She loves that cavalry colonel, because he's a good rider...

celestial.definition: a. of or relating to the sky\na. relating to or inhabiting a divine heaven\ns. of heaven or the spirit
celestial.translation: a. 天的, 天国的, 天空的\n[法] 天的, 天空的, 天国的

examples.en: The solar system is a small celestial system in the Milky Way.
examples.zh: 太阳系是银河系中一个小的天体系统。

examples.en: It is said that Peng Zu was the grandson of a celestial emperor.
examples.zh: 传说彭祖是天帝的孙子。

censor.definition: n. someone who censures or condemns\nn. a person who is authorized to read publications or correspondence or to watch theatrical performances and suppress in whole or in part anything considered obscene or politically unacceptable\nv. subject to political, religious, or moral censorship
censor.translation: n. 检查员\nvt. 检查, 审查, 删改

examples.en: I wonder which country will be the first to censor Tatoeba.
examples.zh: 我想知道哪个国家会第一个和谐Tatoeba？

ceramic.definition: n. an artifact made of hard brittle material produced from nonmetallic minerals by firing at high temperatures\na. of or relating to or made from a ceramic
ceramic.translation: a. 陶瓷的\nn. 陶瓷制品

examples.en: I have an interest in oriental ceramics.
examples.zh: 我对东方陶瓷有兴趣。

chancellor.definition: n. the person who is head of state (in several countries)\nn. the honorary or titular head of a university
chancellor.translation: n. 大臣, 总理, 首相, 大使馆/领事馆的一等秘书, 司法官, 大学校长

examples.en: Hitler was appointed Chancellor by Paul von Hindenburg, a conservative.
The Chancellor of the Exchequer has offered to resign.
The lady was the Federal Chancellor for sixteen years.

changeable.definition: a. such that alteration is possible; having a marked tendency to change\ns. subject to change\ns. varying in color when seen in different lights or from different angles

examples.en: A woman is ever fickle and changeable.
examples.zh: 女人薄情善变。

chant.definition: n. a repetitive song in which as many syllables as necessary are assigned to a single tone\nv. recite with musical intonation; recite as a chant or a psalm
chant.translation: n. 圣歌, 赞美诗\nv. 吟唱, 诵扬

examples.en: Tom and Mary chant the narrative of mainstream media.
Gunter started to chant in some weird language.
The crowd was chanting for Vladimir and Anna to kiss.

chapel.definition: n. a place of worship that has its own altar
chapel.translation: n. 小教堂, 礼拜式

examples.en: Tessa shared her experience in a chapel assembly this April.
examples.zh: 今年四月，苔丝在教会集会上分享了她的经验。

characterization.definition: n. the act of describing distinctive characteristics or essential features
characterization.translation: n. 特性描述, 人物之塑造\n[建] 特性因数

examples.en: The theater company's characterization of Anne Frank was very emotional, but tasteful.
I don't think that's a very accurate characterization of his point of view.
Critics may argue that all the foregoing characterizations are very abstract.

charcoal.definition:
n. a carbonaceous material obtained by heating wood or other organic matter in the absence of air
n. a stick of black carbon material used for drawing
n. a very dark grey color
n. a drawing made with a stick of black carbon material

examples.en: Tom does not know the difference between charcoal and carbon.
examples.zh: Tom不知道碳和煤的差别。

charisma.definition: n. a personal attractiveness or interestingness that enables you to influence others
charisma.translation: n. 非凡的领导力, 神秘的个人魅力, 神授的能力

examples.en: The stage charisma of drag performers compels audiences to reconsider their own stereotypes.
examples.zh: 反串秀者的舞台魅力使观众不禁重新审视自己的刻板印象。

examples.en: You underestimate your charisma.
examples.zh: 你低估了你的魅力。

charitable.definition: a. relating to or characterized by charity\na. full of love and generosity\ns. showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
charitable.translation: a. 大慈大悲的, 宽厚的, 慈善的\n[法] 慈善的, 慷慨的, 宽恕的

examples.en: Members of the evangelical faith often engage in charitable activities.
Although his intention is charitable, it does more harm than good.
Although her intention is charitable, it does more harm than good.

cherish.definition: v be fond of; be attached to
cherish.translation: vt. 珍爱, 怀有, 爱护

examples.en: Cherish our cultural relics; it is all our duty.
examples.zh: 爱护文物, 人人有责。

examples.en: I still cherish the necklace you gave me ten years ago.
examples.zh: 我至今还珍惜你十年前给我的项链。

examples.en: One must understand and cherish fortune before creating it.
examples.zh: 人要知福、惜福、再造福。

chili.definition: n. ground beef and chili peppers or chili powder often with tomatoes and kidney beans\nn. very hot and finely tapering pepper of special pungency
chili.translation: n. 干辣椒, 辣椒粉

examples.en: Taste the sauce to see if it needs more chili.
I'll give you the same amount of chili to eat.
My love, I'm making a chili pie for your mother.

chimney.definition: n. a vertical flue that provides a path through which smoke from a fire is carried away through the wall or roof of a building
chimney.translation: n. 烟囱, 灯罩\n[电] 烟囱

examples.en: Tom is clambering about on the roof, repairing the chimney stack.
examples.zh: 汤姆在屋顶一边爬一边修理烟囱。

examples.en: The smoke went upward through the chimney.
examples.zh: 烟从烟囱里冒了出来。

examples.en: Smoke is rising from the chimney.
examples.zh: 烟从烟囱上升。

chord.definition: n. a straight line connecting two points on a curve\nn. a combination of three or more notes that blend harmoniously when sounded together\nv. play chords on (a string instrument)
chord.translation: n. 弦, 和音\n[医] 索, 带

examples.en: The piano is a chord instrument, while the flute is a monophonic instrument.
examples.zh: 钢琴是和弦乐器，笛子是单音乐器。

examples.en: I can't quite figure out what that chord around 1:58 is. Can somebody help me out?
examples.zh: 我听来听去也听不到一分五十八秒左右的那个和弦是甚么和弦，有人可以帮帮我吗？

chore.definition: n a specific piece of work required to be done as a duty or for a specific fee
chore.translation: n. 零工, 家务\n[经] 零工

examples.en: More and more married couples share household chores.
examples.zh: 夫妻分担家务的情况愈来愈普遍。

choreography.definition: n. the representation of dancing by symbols as music is represented by notes\nn. a notation used by choreographers
choreography.translation: n. 舞蹈艺术, 舞台舞蹈

examples.en: I enjoyed the flashy choreography used in the musical.
Mary designed the choreography for her own performance.
I'm not a fan of the choreography.

chuckle.definition: v. laugh quietly or with restraint
chuckle.translation: n. 咯咯的笑声, 轻笑\nvi. 咯咯的笑, 咕咕叫

examples.en: Mary chuckled to herself.
examples.zh: 玛丽暗自发笑。

chunk.translation: n. 大块, 矮胖的人(或物)\n[经] 定样

examples.en: That boy threw a chunk of stone.
examples.zh: 那个男孩抛了一块石头。

circumference.definition: n. the size of something as given by the distance around it\nn. the boundary line encompassing an area or object\nn. the length of the closed curve of a circle
circumference.translation: n. 圆周, 周缘, 胸围\n[医] 周缘, 环状面

examples.en: Is it possible to determine the diameter from the circumference?
examples.zh: 用圆周能不能求得直径？

civic.definition: a. of or relating or belonging to a city
civic.translation: a. 市的, 市民的, 公民的\n[法] 公民的, 市民的, 公民资格的

examples.en: Because of coronavirus, civic life is shutting down in Algeria.
I believe it to be my civic duty.
It's your civic duty to vote.

clad.definition: s. having an outer covering especially of thin metal
clad.translation: vt. 在金属外包上另一种金属\na. 包层金属的\nclothe的过去式和过去分词

examples.en: Mary is scantily clad.
examples.zh: 玛丽著装暴露。

clam.definition: n. burrowing marine mollusk living on sand or mud; the shell closes with viselike firmness\nn. flesh of either hard-shell or soft-shell clams\nv. gather clams, by digging in the sand by the ocean
clam.translation: n. 蛤, 沉默寡言的人\nvi. 捞蛤

examples.en: He'll be happy as a clam at high tide.
The largest kind of clam is the giant clam.
Every time I think of asking her out, I clam up.

clamp.definition: n. a device (generally used by carpenters) that holds things firmly together\nv. fasten or fix with a clamp\nv. impose or inflict forcefully
clamp.translation: n. 夹钳\nvt. 夹紧, 强加

examples.en: A wise businessman knows how to clamp down on costs.
Ziri used a clamp on the workbench for stability.
Ziri asked Yazid if he could borrow his quick grip clamp.

clan.definition: n group of people related by blood or marriage
clan.translation: n. 氏族, 宗族, 集团\n[医] 支

examples.en: The clan system is a key component of traditional Chinese culture.
examples.zh: 宗族制度是中国传统文化的重要组成部分。

clatter.definition: n. a rattling noise (often produced by rapid movement)\nv. make a rattling sound
clatter.translation: n. 咔嗒声, 哗啦声, 嘈杂的谈笑声\nvi. 发出哗啦声, 喧闹的谈笑\nvt. 使咔嗒咔嗒地响

examples.en: The clatter of the horse's hooves soothed him.
The rain clattered on the roof of the bus shelter.
An aeroplane passed overhead, and then the 12.15 train clattered by.

clergy.definition: n. in Christianity, clergymen collectively (as distinguished from the laity)
clergy.translation: n. 牧师, 僧侣, 神职人员

examples.en: People who work for a given faith are called clergy.
All the clergy are against the new law.
Bishops, archbishops and abbots composed the high clergy.

cliche.definition: n a trite or obvious remark
cliche.translation: n. 陈腔滥调, 凸印版\na. 陈腐的

examples.en: The cream exploded into a cliche in the author's coffee mug.
With her green eye shadow and rabbit fur coat, Mary was cliche.
It's a cliche, but it's true.

clientele.translation: n. 诉讼委托人, 客户\n[法] 委托人, 受保护者, 门徒

examples.en: The majority of his clientele are poor people.
examples.zh: 他的客人多是穷人。

clinch.definition:
n. (boxing) the act of one boxer holding onto the other to avoid being hit and to rest momentarily
n. a small slip noose made with seizing
n. the flattened part of a nail or bolt or rivet
v. secure or fasten by flattening the ends of nails or bolts
clinch.translation: n. 钉牢\nv. 敲弯, 用臂钳住

examples.en: Now is the time to clinch the deal.
You could tell they were angry by the clinching of their fists.
He clinched the election when he came out against a tax increase.

clockwise.definition: a. in the same direction as the rotating hands of a clock\nr. in the direction that the hands of a clock move
clockwise.translation: a. 顺时针方向的\nadv. 顺时针方向地

examples.en: You must turn the faucet clockwise to close it.
Do you have to turn it clockwise or counter-clockwise?
How do you tighten a screw, clockwise or anticlockwise?

closet.definition: n. a small private room for study or prayer\nv. confine to a small space, as for intensive work
closet.translation: n. 壁橱, 小室\na. 秘密的, 空谈的\nvt. 把...关入小室

examples.en: Tom hung his jacket in the hall closet.
examples.zh: 汤姆把夹克挂在大厅衣柜里。

examples.en: The burglar shut the child in the closet.
examples.zh: 强盗把小孩关在了衣柜里。

examples.en: Coming out of the closet requires tremendous courage.
examples.zh: 出柜需要莫大的勇气。

clot.definition: n. a lump of material formed from the content of a liquid\nv. change from a liquid to a thickened or solid state\nv. cause to change from a liquid to a solid or thickened state
clot.translation: n. 凝块, 一团\nv. (使)凝结, (使)聚集

examples.en: "I knocked over a tin of paint." "You clumsy clot!"
He has a suspected blood clot and needs medical attention.
The surgeon removed the clot responsible for the vessel's occlusion.

coax.definition: n a transmission line for high-frequency signals\nv influence or urge by gentle urging, caressing, or flattering
coax.translation: vt. 哄, 诱骗, 耐心地摆弄\nvi. 哄骗\n[计] 同轴电缆

examples.en: I don't want to coax you out with kind words.
A plan was devised to coax him out of hiding.
Yanni tried to coax Skura into sending him money.

cocktail.definition: n. a short mixed drink\nn. an appetizer served as a first course at a meal
cocktail.translation: n. 鸡尾酒, 开味品\na. 鸡尾酒会的

examples.en: You can decorate the cocktail with a cherry or a pineapple.
examples.zh: 你可以用一个樱桃或菠萝来装饰这杯鸡尾酒。

examples.en: Lukas was at a cocktail party.
examples.zh: 卢卡斯在鸡尾酒派对。

codify.definition: v. organize into a code or system, such as a body of law
codify.translation: vt. 编成法典\n[法] 使成文法化, 编成法典, 编纂

examples.en: Laws are the codified intolerance of the majority.
The pamphlet codified the movement's political goals and their method of achieving them.
Who codified the rules of football?

coerce.definition: v. to cause to do through pressure or necessity, by physical, moral or intellectual means :"She forced him to take a job in the city"

examples.en: Someone was coerced to kill the politician.
examples.zh: 有人被胁迫要杀这个政治家。

coffin.definition: n. box in which a corpse is buried or cremated\nv. place into a coffin
coffin.translation: n. 棺材, 灵柩\nvt. 把...装进棺材

examples.en: The poor sales during that Holiday season served as the final nail in the coffin for Boar Corporation.
examples.zh: 那个假期销售业绩不佳，为博尔公司敲下了最后一根棺材钉。

cogent.translation: a. 使人首肯的, 使人信服的, 中肯切题的\n[法] 有说服力的, 无法反驳的

examples.en: It's not the most cogent argument.

coincidental.definition: s occurring or operating at the same time
coincidental.translation: a. 一致的, 符合的, 巧合的

examples.en: I am not writing about myself. Any similarity is purely coincidental.
Any resemblance to real persons, living or dead, is purely coincidental.
There's an opinion that such "coincidences" are not coincidental at all.

collateral.definition:
n. a security pledged for the repayment of a loan
a. descended from a common ancestor but through different lines
s. serving to support or corroborate
s. accompany, concomitant
collateral.translation: a. 并行的, 附随的, 旁系的\nn. 旁系亲属, 担保品

examples.en: We'll use the house as collateral so we can borrow some money.
Collateral damage caused by the strikes is fueling militancy in the region.
"Collateral damage" is a euphemism for killing innocent people to protect capital.

colloquial.definition: s. characteristic of informal spoken language or conversation
colloquial.translation: a. 会话的, 口语的, 口语体的

examples.en: He went to France to brush up his colloquial French.
He traveled to France to brush up his colloquial French.
He is unfamiliar with the colloquial register of the language.

colonial.definition:
n. a resident of a colony
a. of or relating to or characteristic of or inhabiting a colony
a. of animals who live in colonies, such as ants
s. composed of many distinct individuals united to form a whole or colony
colonial.translation: a. 殖民的, 殖民地的\n[法] 殖民地居民

examples.en: In the 15th century, Portugal was a great colonial power.
In the 15th century, Portugal was a major colonial power.
Ilan Pappe says that Zionism is a settler colonial movement.

colonize.definition: v. settle as a colony; of countries in the developing world\nv. settle as colonists or establish a colony (in)
colonize.translation: vi. 开拓殖民地\nvt. 殖民于, 移植于

examples.en: Mars will be colonized.
examples.zh: 火星将被殖民。

examples.en: When Spain colonized the Philippines, they were administrated by Mexico City. So it was Mexican Spanish, not Castilian Spanish, that influenced Tagalog.
examples.zh: 当西班牙殖民了菲律宾时，是从墨西哥城管理它的。于是他加禄语是收到了墨西哥式西班牙语的影响，而不卡斯蒂利亚式的。

colossal.definition: s. so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe
colossal.translation: a. 巨大的, 巨像似的

examples.en: The completion of the Suez canal was a colossal achievement.
Katrina, however, cannot compare to a colossal hurricane on Saturn.
Our marriage turned out to be a colossal flop.

commemorate.definition: v. mark by some ceremony or observation\nv. call to remembrance; keep alive the memory of someone or something, as in a ceremony\nv. be or provide a memorial to a person or an event

examples.en: The Dragon Boat Festival commemorates Qu Yuan.
examples.zh: 端午节是纪念屈原的。

examples.en: The statue of the Minute Man commemorates the valiant soldiers who fought in the Revolutionary War.
examples.zh: 民兵雕像是为了纪念独立战争中英勇作战的士兵。

commend.definition:
v. express approval of
v. present as worthy of regard, kindness, or confidence
v. give to in charge
v. express a good opinion of
commend.translation: vt. 嘉奖, 委托给, 推荐

examples.en: Mark is so honest that everybody commends him for it.
examples.zh: 马克是如此的诚实所以每个人都赞扬他。

commonplace.definition: s. completely ordinary and unremarkable\ns. not challenging; dull and lacking excitement
commonplace.translation: n. 寻常事, 老生常谈, 普通的东西\na. 平凡的, 普通的

examples.en: Space travel will be commonplace some time in the future.
examples.zh: 太空旅行终有一天会成为平常事。

examples.en: Rice and noodles are commonplace in Chinese cuisine.
examples.zh: 中餐常有米饭或面条。

examples.en: Space travel will one day become commonplace.
examples.zh: 太空旅行终有一天会成为平常事。

communal.definition: s. for or by a group rather than individuals\na. relating to a small administrative district or community
communal.translation: a. 公有的, 公社的\n[法] 公共的, 自治体的, 巴黎公社的

examples.en: Vladimir takes care of this small communal piece of land.
The apartment is cheap, but it only has communal bathrooms.
What happens if someone refuses to pay the communal expenses?

commune.definition:
n. the smallest administrative district of several European countries
n. a body of people or families living together and sharing everything
v. communicate intimately with; be in a state of heightened, intimate receptivity
v. receive Communion, in the Catholic church
commune.translation: n. 恳谈, 社区, 公社\nvi. 亲密交谈, (感情上)融为一体

examples.en: Tom and Mary lived in a commune in the 1970s.
Sami went to church to commune with fellow Christians.
Tifrit At Umalek is a commune that has given many artists.

commuter.definition: n. a passenger train that is ridden primarily by passengers who travel regularly from one place to another\nn. someone who travels regularly from home in a suburb to work in a city
commuter.translation: n. 乘公共车辆上下班者, 月季票乘客\n[经] 非(当地)居民

examples.en: Mr Smith forgot to take his commuter ticket.
Where can I find a commuter bus?
Commuters were deprived of their transport by the strike.

compact.definition:
n. a small cosmetics case with a mirror; to be carried in a woman's purse
n. a small and economical car
v. have the property of being packable or of compacting easily
a. closely and firmly united or packed together
compact.translation: a. 紧凑的, 紧密的, 简洁的\nvt. 使紧密结合, 压缩\nvi. 变坚实

examples.en: Compact discs have entirely taken the place of phonograph records.
examples.zh: CD已经完全取代了胶木唱片。

examples.en: I want a compact car with an air conditioner.
examples.zh: 我想要一辆有空调的小型车。

examples.en: She gave me this compact disc.
examples.zh: 她给了我这个光碟。

comparable.definition: a. able to be compared or worthy of comparison\ns. conforming in every respect
comparable.translation: a. 可比较的, 比得上的

examples.en: As you know, life is comparable to a voyage.
A comparable car would cost far more in Japan.
They're not comparable — the original knocks the spots off the copyists.

compartment.definition: n. a space into which an area is subdivided\nn. a partitioned section, chamber, or separate room within a larger enclosed area
compartment.translation: n. 分隔间, 卧车包房, 防水舱隔\n[医] 隔室, 隔间

examples.en: I found the secret compartment quite by accident.
examples.zh: 我完全是在偶然的情况下发现了密室。

compassion.definition: n. a deep awareness of and sympathy for another's suffering\nn. the humane quality of understanding the suffering of others and wanting to do something about it

examples.en: A little bit of compassion can go a long way.
I'm shocked at Tom's sheer lack of empathy and compassion.
However, the goddess of the fairies felt compassion for her.

compatible.definition: a. able to exist and perform in harmonious or agreeable combination\na. capable of being used with or connected to other devices or components without modification\ns. capable of forming a homogeneous mixture that neither separates nor is altered by chemical interaction
compatible.translation: a. 能共处的, 可并立的, 适合的\n[计] 相容的; 兼容的

examples.en: Can you find a compatible cartridge for the faucet model?
It's because they're compatible that they get along so well.
A translation widget compatible with the Safari browser is required.

compelling.definition: s. driving or forcing\ns. tending to persuade by forcefulness of argument
compelling.translation: a. 强制的, 强迫性的, 激发兴趣的

examples.en: Green towns enhance your well-being, compelling you to give back.
The defense attorney presented compelling evidence of her client's innocence.
This is a very interesting, intriguing, and compelling story.

compensatory.definition: a. Serving for compensation; making amends.
compensatory.translation: a. 赔偿的, 补偿的, 代偿的\n[医] 代偿的, 补偿的

examples.en: Blind people sometimes develop a compensatory ability to sense the proximity of objects around them.
examples.zh: 某些失明者会产生一个弥补性的能力，这个能力让他们察觉到他们与离他们很近的物体的距离。

complacent.definition: s. contented to a fault with oneself or one's actions
