complacent.translation: a. 满足的, 自满的, 得意的

examples.en: If you knew what I knew, you wouldn't be so complacent.
We should acknowledge that things have improved, but we shouldn't be complacent.
Skura's husband has become a little complacent.

complexion.definition:
n. the coloring of a person's face
n. a combination that results from coupling or interlinking
n. a point of view or general attitude or inclination
n. texture and appearance of the skin of the face
complexion.translation: n. 肤色, 情况, 局面\n[医] 体质; 面色, 面容

examples.en: It was her fearfully pale complexion that caught his eye.
His skin complexion was pale due to his fever.
She's got a fair complexion while her brother is very dark.

compliance.definition: n acting according to certain accepted standards\nn a disposition or tendency to yield to the will of others\nn the act of submitting; usually surrendering power to another
compliance.translation: n. 遵从, 顺从, 屈从\n[化] 柔顺; 顺应

examples.en: We are building your house in compliance with your wishes.
I've brought the website into compliance with W3C standards.
Compliance with a robber's demands does not guarantee your safety.

compliant.definition: a. disposed or willing to comply
compliant.translation: a. 顺从的, 屈从的\n[电] 适用于, 配合...使用

examples.en: According to custom, the bride should be compliant.
examples.zh: 根据习俗，新娘应该循规蹈矩。

composite.definition: n. considered the most highly evolved dicotyledonous plants, characterized by florets arranged in dense heads that resemble single flowers\ns. consisting of separate interconnected parts\na. of or relating to or belonging to the plant family Compositae
composite.translation: a. 合成的, 混合成的, 菊科的\nn. 合成物, 复合材料, 菊科

examples.en: Composite materials represent a sea change in the aerospace industry.
A Portuguese man o' war is a composite of four animals.
This ghost photo is well made, but it's just a composite.

compost.definition: n. a mixture of decaying vegetation and manure; used as a fertilizer\nv. convert to compost
compost.translation: n. 混合物, 堆肥\nvt. 施堆肥于

examples.en: Dispose of food scraps properly in the compost or trash.
All the organic matter in the compost pile is decomposing.
Tom's compost heap got so hot that it spontaneously combusted.

compulsive.definition: n. a person with a compulsive disposition; someone who feels compelled to do certain things\ns. caused by or suggestive of psychological compulsion\ns. strongly motivated to succeed
compulsive.translation: a. 强制的, 强迫的\n[医] 强迫性的

examples.en: My husband is a compulsive gambler. What can I do?
The therapist is treating the patient for compulsive masturbation.
I know that Tom is a compulsive liar.

concave.translation: a. 凹的\n[医] 凹的, 凹面的

examples.en: You will need a concave lens to take those photos.
The moon's orbit is always concave toward the sun.
Concave is the antonym of convex.

conceited.definition: s. characteristic of false pride; having an exaggerated sense of self-importance
conceited.translation: a. 自负的, 逞能的, 狂想的

examples.en: Tom told Mary that he didn't think John was conceited.
Tom isn't as conceited as he used to be.
Mary isn't as conceited as she used to be.

conceptual.definition: s. being or characterized by concepts or their formation
conceptual.translation: a. 概念的\n[医] 概念的

examples.en: The Econ exam was pretty easy, mostly conceptual stuff, supply and demand, and all that.

concession.definition: n. a contract granting the right to operate a subsidiary business\nn. the act of conceding or yielding\nn. a point conceded or yielded
concession.translation: n. 特许, 让步, 认可\n[经] 核准, 许可, 特殊(权)

examples.en: We would appreciate it if you grant us this concession.
Please let us know your conditions for making the concession.
Tom works at a movie theater concession stand.

concise.definition: a. expressing much in few words
concise.translation: a. 简洁的, 简明的

examples.en: Either one is fine, but the former is more concise.
examples.zh: 两者都可以，但是前者更简洁。

examples.en: His comment was concise and to the point.
examples.zh: 他的评论简洁且击中要害。

examples.en: I find words with concise definitions to be the easiest to remember.
examples.zh: 我发现有明确定义的词最容易记住。

conclusive.definition: a. forming an end or termination; especially putting an end to doubt or question
conclusive.translation: a. 决定性的, 确定性的, 最后的\n[法] 决定性的, 不容置疑的, 确实的

examples.en: There has been no conclusive proof regarding extra-sensory perception.
This horrible mistake led to Tom's conclusive dismissal.
The evidence is fairly conclusive.

condensation.definition: n. (psychoanalysis) an unconscious process whereby two ideas or images combine into a single symbol; especially in dreams\nn. the process of changing from a gaseous to a liquid or solid state\nn. atmospheric moisture that has condensed because of cold
condensation.translation: n. 压缩, 凝缩, 冷凝\n[化] 冷凝; 冷凝作用; 缩合; 缩合作用; 凝聚; 凝聚作用; 凝结作用

examples.en: Tom grabbed a squeegee to wipe the condensation off the windshield.
Rivulets of condensation ran down the draughty windows.
The windows are misted up with condensation.

condense.definition:
v. undergo condensation; change from a gaseous to a liquid state and fall in drops
v. remove water from
v. cause a gas or vapor to change into a liquid
v. become more compact or concentrated
condense.translation: vt. 使浓缩, 使压缩, 缩短\nvi. 浓缩, 凝结

examples.en: It's hard to condense this into a short article.
Clouds are clusters of water droplets condensed from water vapor.
Do you drink coffee with condensed milk or without?

condolence.definition: n. an expression of sympathy with another's grief

examples.en: When his wife died, he received dozens of condolence cards.
We send our condolences for the loss of your aunt.
Please accept my condolences on the death of your father.

cone.definition:
n. any cone-shaped artifact
n. a shape whose base is a circle and whose sides taper up to a point
n. cone-shaped mass of ovule- or spore-bearing scales or bracts
n. a visual receptor cell in the retina that is sensitive to bright light and to color
cone.translation: n. 圆锥体, 球果\nvt. 使成锥形

examples.en: Jane wanted an ice cream cone.
examples.zh: 珍想要一个冰淇淋甜筒。

examples.en: Tom collected some pine cones in the forest.
examples.zh: 汤姆在森林里捡了一些松果。

confederation.definition: n. a union of political organizations\nn. the act of forming an alliance or confederation
confederation.translation: n. 同盟, 联盟, 组织联盟

examples.en: Liechtenstein became fully independent in 1866 when the Confederation dissolved.
The Holy Roman Empire was a confederation of princely states in Germany.
The Swiss Confederation secured its independence from the Holy Roman Empire in 1499.

configuration.definition: n. an arrangement of parts or elements
configuration.translation: n. 结构, 表面配置, 外形, 配置\n[计] 配置

examples.en: Tom's face detected an unsupported facial hair configuration.
We were running out of disk space due to a configuration issue.
The configuration file for your database server is located in this directory.

confiscate.translation: vt. 没收, 把...充公, 查抄\na. 被没收的

examples.en: The teacher confiscated a student's phone because he was texting in class.
examples.zh: 老师没收了一个学生的手机，因为他在课上发短信。

examples.en: The package was confiscated by customs.
examples.zh: 包裹被海关扣了。

congregation.definition: n. a group of people who adhere to a common faith and habitually attend a given church\nn. an assemblage of people or animals or things collected together\nn. the act of congregating
congregation.translation: n. 集合, 聚集\n[法] 集会, 人一, 红衣主教会议

examples.en: Sami was described as a beloved pastor by his congregation.
Sami is very well respected and beloved in the congregation.
Ziri left and the rest of the congregation followed.

conjunction.definition: n. an uninflected function word that serves to conjoin words or phrases or clauses or sentences\nn. the grammatical relation between linguistic units (words or phrases or clauses) that are connected by a conjunction\nn. (astronomy) apparent meeting or passing of two or more celestial bodies in the same degree of the zodiac
conjunction.translation: n. 连接词, 联合, 结合\n[计] 合取

examples.en: A conjunction is an invariable word that links two ideas.
Bribes are something that arises in conjunction with power organizations.
Private companies have been working in conjunction with local communities.

consecutive.definition: s. in regular succession without gaps\nr. in a consecutive manner
consecutive.translation: a. 连续的, 联贯的\n[计] 连续的; 连接的

examples.en: It snowed for ten consecutive days.
examples.zh: 雪持续下了十天。

console.definition: n. a scientific instrument consisting of displays and an input device that an operator can use to monitor and control a system (especially a computer system)\nn. an ornamental scroll-shaped bracket (especially one used to support a wall fixture)
console.translation: vt. 安慰, 藉慰\nn. 控制台\n[计] 控制台

examples.en: She tried to console him.
examples.zh: 她试著安慰他。

examples.en: Who will console me?
examples.zh: 谁来安慰我？

examples.en: Who will console her?
examples.zh: 谁去安慰她？

conspicuous.definition: a. obvious to the eye or mind
conspicuous.translation: a. 显著的, 显眼的, 出众的

examples.en: The scar on his forehead is conspicuous.
examples.zh: 他额头上的疤痕很醒目。

constrain.translation: vt. 强迫, 限制, 关押

examples.en: What human trespass would constrain thy power, O Zeus?
We are constrained to and restrained from an action.
The government finances are severely constrained because of falling tax revenues.

consul.definition: n. a diplomat appointed by a government to protect its commercial interests and help its citizens in a foreign country
consul.translation: n. 领事, 执政官\n[经] 领事

examples.en: After he was chosen as consul, Scipio was sent to Africa.
He came to Rome while Marius was consul.
Do not say anything, please, about your consul.

consultation.definition: n. a conference (usually with someone important)\nn. a conference between two or more people to consider a particular question
consultation.translation: n. 请教, 咨询, 磋商会\n[医] 会诊

examples.en: I had a consultation with a lawyer about my will.
The plan was made in consultation with the Algerian government.
I'd like to have a consultation about getting braces.

contagious.definition: s. easily diffused or spread as from one person to another
contagious.translation: a. 触染性的, 会蔓延的\n[医] (接)触(传)染的

examples.en: Enthusiasm is contagious.
examples.zh: 热情具有传染性。

contemptuous.translation: a. 轻蔑的, 鄙视的, 瞧不起人的

examples.en: Adolf Eichmann hated rules and was contemptuous of bureaucracy.
He is contemptuous of his boss's narrow mind.
Tom seems to be contemptuous of ordinary people.

contentious.definition: s. inclined or showing an inclination to dispute or disagree, even to engage in law suits\ns. involving or likely to cause controversy
contentious.translation: a. 好争吵的, 爱争论的, 有异议的\n[法] 诉讼的, 争执的, 引起争论的

examples.en: The issue turned out to be very contentious.
Religion is a contentious topic for many people.
The debate was very contentious and didn't result in any fruitful conclusions.

contingency.definition: n. the state of being contingent on something
contingency.translation: n. 偶然性, 可能性, 意外事故\n[经] 意外事故, 意外开支, 偶然事故

examples.en: Do you have a contingency plan in place?
The president's lack of a defined contingency plan is maladroit at best.
Does the army have a contingency plan?

contraception.definition: n. birth control by the use of devices (diaphragm or intrauterine device or condom) or drugs or surgery
contraception.translation: n. 避孕, 避孕法\n[医] 节(制生)育, 避孕

examples.en: What methods of contraception are you using?
examples.zh: 你们采取什么措施避孕？

convergence.definition: n. the occurrence of two or more things coming together\nn. the approach of an infinite series to a finite limit\nn. the act of converging (coming closer)
convergence.translation: n. 集中, 收敛\n[计] 收敛, 会聚

converse.definition:
n. a proposition obtained by conversion
v. carry on a conversation
s. of words so related that one reverses the relation denoted by the other
s. turned about in order or relation
converse.translation: n. 相反的事物, 倒, 逆向\na. 相反的, 逆向的, 颠倒的\nvi. 交谈, 谈话

examples.en: It was nice to converse with her.
examples.zh: 和她交谈很愉快。

examples.en: The two met entirely by chance. Being of similar age and appearance, they quickly found themselves admiring one another as they conversed.
examples.zh: 他两个萍水相逢，年相若，貌相似，谭吐应对之间，彼此敬慕。

coral.definition:
n. a variable color averaging a deep pink
n. the hard stony skeleton of a Mediterranean coral that has a delicate red or pink color and is used for jewelry
n. unfertilized lobster roe; reddens in cooking; used as garnish or to color sauces
n. marine colonial polyp characterized by a calcareous skeleton; masses in a variety of shapes often forming reefs
coral.translation: n. 珊瑚, 珊瑚色\n[化] 珊瑚

examples.en: The coral reef is the region's prime attraction.
examples.zh: 珊瑚礁是这个地区的主要景点。

coronary.definition: a. surrounding like a crown (especially of the blood vessels surrounding the heart)
coronary.translation: a. 冠的, 花冠的, 冠状的\n[医] 冠状的

examples.en: I've got a bad heart: coronary artery disease.
I've got a bum ticker: coronary artery disease.
The doctor explained that angina is a common symptom of underlying coronary artery disease.

corporal.definition: n. a noncommissioned officer in the Army or Air Force or Marines
corporal.translation: n. 下士\na. 肉体的, 身体的, 个人的

examples.en: Personally, I think that corporal punishment is a necessary evil.
The trend of public opinion is against corporal punishment.
I remember when corporal punishment was allowed in schools.

corps.definition: n. an army unit usually consisting of two or more divisions and their support\nn. a body of people associated together
corps.translation: n. 军, 队, 部队, 兵种\n[医] 对, 团; 体, 物体

examples.en: Whoever demands something instantly doesn't belong to the diplomatic corps.
Our town does not have a corps of firemen.
Ziri has finished his years at the Marine Corps.

corpse.definition: n the dead body of a human being

examples.en: Every man is a potential corpse.
examples.zh: 每个人都可能变成尸体。

corpus.definition: n. a collection of writings\nn. the main part of an organ or other bodily structure
corpus.translation: n. (事物的)主体, 文集, 本金, 语料库\n[医] 体

examples.en: This is a corpus of example sentences in various languages.
How many one-word Hungarian sentences are there in the corpus?
This corpus is just a giant compilation of independent clauses.

cosmetic.definition: n. a toiletry designed to beautify the body\ns. serving an esthetic rather than a useful purpose\ns. serving an aesthetic purpose in beautifying the body
cosmetic.translation: n. 化妆品\na. 化妆用的

examples.en: Cosmetic surgery is not covered by most insurance plans.
examples.zh: 大部份的保险计划不包含整容手术。

cosmic.definition: a. of or from or pertaining to or characteristic of the cosmos or universe\ns. inconceivably extended in space or time
cosmic.translation: a. 宇宙的, 宇宙航行的, 无限的, 有秩序的\n[医] 宇宙的

examples.en: If the universe is a cosmic egg, who laid it?
How much cosmic radiation reaches earth during the solar minimum?
Why is the cosmic web the way it is?

cosmopolitan.definition:
n. a sophisticated person who has travelled in many countries
a. growing or occurring in many parts of the world
a. composed of people from or at home in many parts of the world; especially not provincial in attitudes or interests
s. of worldwide scope or applicability
cosmopolitan.translation: a. 世界主义的, 世界性的, 全世界的, 遍生的, 不偏狭的, 卓有见识的\nn. 世界主义者, 世界性

examples.en: The journalist is what you call a cosmopolitan.
Some cities are very cosmopolitan. Others, less so.
Tom drank a Long Island iced tea and Mary drank a cosmopolitan.

cosmos.definition: n. any of various mostly Mexican herbs of the genus Cosmos having radiate heads of variously colored flowers and pinnate leaves; popular fall-blooming annuals
cosmos.translation: n. 宇宙, 秩序, 和谐, 大波斯菊\n[医] 大波斯菊

examples.en: To date nobody knows the actual size of the cosmos.
examples.zh: 宇宙的实际大小至今无人知道。

examples.en: The telescope has opened a new eye onto the cosmos that has been transformative for our civilization.
examples.zh: 望远镜为我们的文明开启了一种全新的视角来观察宇宙。

counterfeit.definition: n. a copy that is represented as the original\na. not genuine; imitating something superior
counterfeit.translation: n. 赝品, 伪造品\na. 假冒的, 假装的\nv. 仿造, 伪装, 假装

examples.en: The most commonly counterfeited medicines in poor countries are used to treat life-threatening conditions such as malaria, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS.
examples.zh: 在贫穷国家，最常见的仿冒药品是用来治疗疟疾、结核病和爱滋病等危及生命的疾病的药品。

coup.definition: n. a brilliant and notable success
coup.translation: n. 砰然的一击, 妙计, 出乎意料的行动, 政变\n[医] 发作, 中, 击

examples.en: The coup d'etat in Brazil is an affront to democracy.
A faction of the Turkish military attempted an anti-Erdogan coup.
The coup attempt was foiled at the last moment.

covenant.definition:
n. a signed written agreement between two or more parties (nations) to perform some action
n. (Bible) an agreement between God and his people in which God makes certain promises and requires certain behavior from them in return
v. enter into a covenant
v. enter into a covenant or formal agreement
covenant.translation: n. 契约, 盟约\nv. 立契约, 缔结盟约

examples.en: The Ark of the Covenant contains the two stone tablets with the Ten Commandments inscribed.
And I will make my covenant between me and thee: and I will multiply thee exceedingly.
There is no Jewish religion separate from the notion of a nation bound to it by covenant.

covert.definition: n. a flock of coots\na. secret or hidden; not openly practiced or engaged in or shown or avowed\ns. (of a wife) being under the protection of her husband
covert.translation: a. 隐蔽的, 偷偷摸摸的, 隐密的\nn. 树丛, 隐藏处

examples.en: The CIA fought a covert war against the Soviets in Afghanistan.
We have been sent on a covert mission.
We’re also exploring technologies that reduce the potential for covert data collection.

crab.definition:
n. decapod having eyes on short stalks and a broad flattened carapace with a small abdomen folded under the thorax and pincers
n. a quarrelsome grouch
n. the edible flesh of any of various crabs
n. a stroke of the oar that either misses the water or digs too deeply
crab.translation: n. 螃蟹, 偏航, 脾气乖戾的人, 沙果\nvi. 捕蟹, 偏航, 发牢骚\nvt. 使偏航, 抱怨, 破坏

examples.en: The first person who ate crab must also have tried to eat a spider.
examples.zh: 第一个吃螃蟹的人一定也吃过蜘蛛。

examples.en: Look, look! On the branch of the orange tree, there is a blue hermit crab!
examples.zh: 快看快看！橙子树的树枝上有一只蓝色的寄居蟹！

cramp.definition:
n. a clamp for holding pieces of wood together while they are glued
n. a strip of metal with ends bent at right angles; used to hold masonry together
v. secure with a cramp
v. affect with or as if with a cramp
cramp.translation: n. 痉挛, 腹部绞痛, 铁夹钳\na. 狭窄的, 难认的\nvt. 使抽筋, 以铁箍扣紧, 束缚

examples.en: I just got another leg cramp and it hurts like hell.
examples.zh: 我刚刚腿又抽筋了，痛死我了。

examples.en: I want to move out of this cramped room as soon as I can.
examples.zh: 我想尽快从这个不透气的屋子里出去。

examples.en: This room is cramped.
examples.zh: 这个房间很拥挤。

crater.definition: n. a faint constellation in the southern hemisphere near Hydra and Corvus\nn. a bowl-shaped depression formed by the impact of a meteorite or bomb
crater.translation: n. 火山口, 环行山, 弹坑\n[化] 焊口; 火山石; 弧坑; 焰口

examples.en: Some of the bluest water in the world is found in Crater Lake.
examples.zh: 一些世界上最蓝的水在火山湖。

crave.definition: v. have a craving, appetite, or great desire for\nv. plead or ask for earnestly
crave.translation: v. 渴望, 热望, 恳求

examples.en: The heat is making me crave for an ice cream.
examples.zh: 热得想吃冰淇淋。

examples.en: As the trees crave tranquility in the ever-persistent wind, the child craves the care of its ever-absent parents.
examples.zh: 树欲静而风不息，子欲养而亲不在！

credential.definition: n a document attesting to the truth of certain stated facts
credential.translation: n. 国书, 凭据, 证明书\n[经] 凭证, 证书

examples.en: An internship is the most important credential for entering the job market.
A credential is something that’s proof of a claim you make about yourself or your skills.

creed.definition: n. any system of principles or beliefs
creed.translation: n. 宗教信条, 教义, 纲领

examples.en: The laws apply to everyone irrespective of race, creed or color.
Shahada is the Muslim creed.
There are no creeds in mathematics.

creek.definition: n. any member of the Creek Confederacy (especially the Muskogee) formerly living in Georgia and Alabama but now chiefly in Oklahoma
creek.translation: n. 小溪, 小河, 小湾

examples.en: There used to be a lot of small creeks in old time Shanghai, which included Zhaojia Creek and Yangjing Creek, but they're all covered up nowadays.
examples.zh: 上海以前有许多小河浜，其中有肇家浜、洋泾浜，现在都被填了。

crest.definition:
n. the top line of a hill, mountain, or wave
n. (heraldry) in medieval times, an emblem used to decorate a helmet
n. a showy growth of e.g. feathers or skin on the head of a bird or other animal
v. reach a high point
crest.translation: n. 冠, 饰毛, 头盔的顶部\nvi. 到达绝顶\nvt. 加以顶饰

examples.en: The surfer tried to ride the crest of the wave.
Tom's guinea pig Cookie has a crest on his head.
The tourist path led along the crest of the mountain.

cringe.definition: v draw back, as with fear or pain\nv show submission or fear
cringe.translation: n. 畏缩, 奉承\nvi. 畏缩, 抖缩, 阿谀

examples.en: I may be cringe, but you're mean, and that's worse.
Why don't you calm down? You're really making me cringe.
At first I cringe, but I want more.

crisp.definition:
s. (of something seen or heard) clearly defined
s. tender and brittle
s. pleasantly cold and invigorating
s. pleasingly firm and fresh
crisp.translation: a. 脆的, 新鲜的, 活泼的\nv. (使)烘脆, (使)拳曲, (使)起皱\nn. 松脆物

examples.en: People will fry to a crisp in the sun today.
Grab the meat before it burns to a crisp!
The salad at Benedito's restaurant is fresh and crisp.

crossroads.definition: n. a point where a choice must be made
crossroads.translation: n. 十字路口, 交叉路口, 聚会的中心地点, (喻)需作抉择的重要关头, 紧要关头

examples.en: There's been an accident at the crossroads.
examples.zh: 十字路口出了车祸。

crouch.definition: n. the act of bending low with the limbs close to the body\nv. bend one's back forward from the waist on down
crouch.translation: n. 蹲伏, 蜷缩\nvi. 蹲下, 蜷着, 缩着\nvt. 低头

examples.en: Mr. Crouch, what are you doing?
examples.zh: Crouch 先生，你在做什么？

examples.en: Not far away, screened by the forest, crouched Shiegra, the lioness, intent upon devouring the infant for her evening meal.
examples.zh: 不远处，母狮谢格拉匍匐著，隐匿于林间，正伺机将婴儿吞食，作为她的晚餐。

crust.definition:
n. the outer layer of the Earth
n. a hard outer layer that covers something
n. the trait of being rude and impertinent; inclined to take liberties
v. form a crust or form into a crust
crust.translation: n. 外壳, 坚硬外皮, 面包皮\nvt. 盖以硬皮\nvi. 结硬皮

examples.en: The snow lay on the ground, frozen into a thick, hard crust.
examples.zh: 地上覆盖着积雪，冻成了又硬又厚的壳。

cub.definition:
n. an awkward and inexperienced youth
n. a male child (a familiar term of address to a boy)
n. the young of certain carnivorous mammals such as the bear or wolf or lion
v. give birth to cubs

examples.en: The tiger cub looked like a large kitten.
examples.zh: 小老虎看起来像只大猫。

examples.en: One may only catch the tiger cub by entering the tiger's den.
examples.zh: 不入虎穴，焉得虎子。

cuisine.definition: n. the practice or manner of preparing food or the food so prepared
cuisine.translation: n. 烹调风格, 烹调法, 烹饪, 厨房

examples.en: This restaurant serves French cuisine, but with Japanese tableware.
examples.zh: 这家餐厅供应法国菜，但使用日式餐具。

examples.en: The Uyghurs' cuisine has all kinds of dishes.
examples.zh: 维族人的饭菜各式各样。

examples.en: Rice and noodles are commonplace in Chinese cuisine.
examples.zh: 中餐常有米饭或面条。

cult.definition:
n. followers of an exclusive system of religious beliefs and practices
n. followers of an unorthodox, extremist, or false religion or sect who often live outside of conventional society under the direction of a charismatic leader
n. a religion or sect that is generally considered to be unorthodox, extremist, or false
n. a system of religious beliefs and rituals
cult.translation: n. 膜拜, 礼拜式, 祭仪, 一群信徒\n[医] 迷信, 巫术

examples.en: Tom didn't know he was getting involved in a cult.
Sami didn't know he was getting involved in a cult.
Sami considers Layla an enemy because she left his cult.

curator.definition: n. the custodian of a collection (as a museum or library)
curator.translation: n. 管理者, 经理, 主管人, 掌管者, 馆长, 大学学监, 监护人, 保护人\n[经] 临时监护人

examples.en: Elena is the curator of a modern art gallery.
Tom is a museum curator.
Mary is a museum curator.

curb.definition: n. an edge between a sidewalk and a roadway consisting of a line of curbstones (usually forming part of a gutter)\nn. a horse's bit with an attached chain or strap to check the horse\nv. keep to the curb
curb.translation: n. 抑制, 勒马绳, 边石\nvt. 抑制, 束缚, 勒住

examples.en: He just uses women and kicks them to the curb.
Sami crossed the road and got to the other curb.
Your car is parked too far from the curb.

curry.definition: n. (East Indian cookery) a pungent dish of vegetables or meats flavored with curry powder and usually eaten with rice\nv. season with a mixture of spices; typical of Indian cooking\nv. treat by incorporating fat
curry.translation: n. 咖哩粉, 咖哩饭菜\nvt. 用咖哩粉调味, 用马梳梳, 制革

examples.en: The curry at this restaurant is good.
examples.zh: 这家饭馆的咖哩挺好。

examples.en: We ate curry rice last night.
examples.zh: 我们昨晚吃了咖哩饭。

examples.en: I ate curry last night.
examples.zh: 我昨晚吃了咖喱。

customary.definition: s. in accordance with convention or custom
customary.translation: a. 习惯的, 惯常的\n[经] 通常的, 习惯的

examples.en: In Asian culture it's customary to take one's shoes off before entering a house or temple.
examples.zh: 在亚洲文化里，习惯在进一个房子或一座寺庙前先脱鞋子。

cynical.definition: s. believing the worst of human nature and motives; having a sneering disbelief in e.g. selflessness of others
cynical.translation: a. 愤世嫉俗的, 讽刺的, 冷嘲的

examples.en: People grow more cynical with age.
examples.zh: 人会随著年龄的增长而更加地玩世不恭。

camel.definition: n. cud-chewing mammal used as a draft or saddle animal in desert regions
camel.translation: n. 骆驼, 打捞浮筒

examples.en: A camel is, so to speak, a ship on the desert.
examples.zh: 骆驼，这么说吧，也就是沙漠中的船。

examples.en: The camel can go a long time without water and food.
examples.zh: 骆驼可以撑很久不吃不喝。

examples.en: A camel is to the desert what a ship is to the sea.
examples.zh: 骆驼是沙漠之舟。

canyon.definition: n. a ravine formed by a river in an area with little rainfall
canyon.translation: n. 峡谷, 海底悬崖

examples.en: Ziri began walking towards Rima's last position in the canyon.
Igor doesn't know how to get to the canyon.
The sound of a gunshot echoed across the canyon.

cemetery.definition: n. a tract of land used for burials
cemetery.translation: n. 墓地, 公墓\n[法] 公墓, 墓地

examples.en: J.F. Kennedy was buried in Arlington Cemetery.
examples.zh: 约翰甘迺迪被安葬在阿灵顿公墓。

cholesterol.definition: n. an animal sterol that is normally synthesized by the liver; the most abundant steroid in animal tissues
cholesterol.translation: n. 胆固醇\n[化] 胆固醇; 胆固醇

examples.en: My cholesterol is high.
examples.zh: 我的胆固醇很高。

chromosome.definition: n. a threadlike strand of DNA in the cell nucleus that carries the genes in a linear order
chromosome.translation: n. 染色体\n[化] 染色体

examples.en: Dogs have 39 pairs of chromosomes.
examples.zh: 狗有39对染色体。

circus.definition:
n. a travelling company of entertainers; including trained animals
n. a performance given by a traveling company of acrobats, clowns, and trained animals
n. a frenetic disorganized (and often comic) disturbance suggestive of a large public entertainment
n. (antiquity) an open-air stadium for chariot races and gladiatorial games
circus.translation: n. 马戏团, 马戏, 竞技场

examples.en: Tom works as an elephant trainer in a circus.
examples.zh: 汤姆在一个马戏团当训象师。

examples.en: At the age of six, I was taken to a circus for the first time.
examples.zh: 在我六岁的时候，我第一次被带去看马戏。

examples.en: That is a circus!
examples.zh: 那是个马戏团！

commissioner.definition: n. a government administrator\nn. a member of a commission
commissioner.translation: n. 委员, 理事, 行政长官\n[法] 委员, 政府的特派员, 地方地官

examples.en: It wasn't I, commissioner!
examples.zh: 局长，那不是我！

examples.en: It wasn't me, commissioner!
examples.zh: 局长，那不是我！

conquest.definition: n. the act of conquering\nn. success in mastering something difficult
conquest.translation: n. 战胜, 征服, 战利品\n[法] 征服, 赢得, 获得

examples.en: Go is a game of dispute and conquest of territory.
The horse is the noblest conquest ever made by man.
Archeologically speaking, there was never any Hebrew conquest of Canaan.

converge.definition:
v. be adjacent or come together
v. approach a limit as the number of terms increases without limit
v. move or draw together at a certain location
v. come together so as to form a single product
converge.translation: vi. 聚合, 集中于一点\nvt. 使集合

examples.en: Godwin's law teaches us that any infinite discussion about an arbitrary subject converges to a Nazi comparison.
examples.zh: 高德温法则告诉我们对任何主题的所有无休止的讨论会趋于和纳粹主义的类比。

corrode.definition: v. cause to deteriorate due to the action of water, air, or an acid\nv. become destroyed by water, air, or a corrosive such as an acid
corrode.translation: vt. 使腐蚀, 侵蚀, 破坏\nvi. 被侵蚀, 起腐蚀作用

examples.en: Dehumanization and racism corrode the moral fabric of society.
The substance can irritate or corrode the skin, eyes, or mucous membranes.
Normalizing hate speech corrodes the moral fabric of society.

costume.definition:
n. the attire worn in a play or at a fancy dress ball
n. unusual or period attire not characteristic of or appropriate to the time and place
n. the prevalent fashion of dress (including accessories and hair style as well as garments)
n. the attire characteristic of a country or a time or a social class

examples.en: Sami was the only one who could fit into the costume.
examples.zh: 萨米是唯一一个能穿上这件衣服的人。

examples.en: He's taken off his mask, torn off his costume. There's no doubt now about what the far-right candidate intends.
examples.zh: 他摘下了面具，卸下了伪装。极右翼候选人的意图已昭然若揭。

courtyard.definition: n an area wholly or partly surrounded by walls or buildings

examples.en: In Beijing, hutongs are alleys formed by lines of siheyuans, the traditional courtyard residences.
examples.zh: 在北京，胡同是由四合院的传统居所排形成。

examples.en: The window overlooks the courtyard.
examples.zh: 窗户俯瞰著院子。

examples.en: No matter how fierce the winds blow or the waves crash, it feels as effortless as strolling leisurely in a quiet courtyard.
examples.zh: 不管风吹浪打，胜似闲庭信步。

caffeine.definition: n. a bitter alkaloid found in coffee and tea that is responsible for their stimulating effects
caffeine.translation: n. 咖啡因, 咖啡碱\n[化] 咖啡因; 咖啡碱

examples.en: Tom has a caffeine dependency, doesn't he?
examples.zh: 汤姆对咖啡因有依赖，是吗？

examples.en: Will you be able to sleep with all that caffeine you've just had?
examples.zh: 你刚进食了那么多咖啡因还睡得了觉吗？

calorie.definition: n. a unit of heat equal to the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of water by one degree at one atmosphere pressure; used by nutritionists to characterize the energy-producing potential in food\nn. unit of heat defined as the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of water by 1 degree centigrade at atmospheric pressure

examples.en: High calorie foods are bad for my health.
examples.zh: 高卡路里的食物对我的身体不好。

canvas.definition:
n. a heavy, closely woven fabric (used for clothing or chairs or sails or tents)
n. an oil painting on canvas fabric
n. the setting for a narrative or fictional or dramatic account
n. the mat that forms the floor of the ring in which boxers or professional wrestlers compete
canvas.translation: n. 帆布, 画布, 油画\n[化] 帆布

examples.en: A new art trend in New York City takes the age-old craft of crocheting to the streets, where traditionally walls and fences have been serving as canvases for graffiti artists.
examples.zh: 纽约市出现了一种新的艺术潮流，将古老的钩编工艺带到了街头。在那里，传统上，墙壁和栅栏一直是涂鸦艺术家的画布。

caravan.definition: n. a procession (of wagons or mules or camels) traveling together in single file\nv. travel in a caravan
caravan.translation: n. 旅行队, 有篷顶的大车\n[经] 商队, 结队商贩

examples.en: A long caravan of camel was heading to the West.
A dog is barking and a caravan is passing.
She can't remember the way to the caravan park.

cardboard.definition: n. a stiff moderately thick paper\ns. without substance
cardboard.translation: n. 薄纸板\n[化] 咭纸; 特等纸板; 卡纸板; 卡片纸板

examples.en: These cardboard boxes are a hundred per cent recyclable.
examples.zh: 这些纸板盒是百分之百可回收的。

examples.en: Prepare five postcard sized pieces of cardboard.
examples.zh: 准备五张明信片大小的硬纸板。

examples.en: Outside the school, she saw people with no homes living in cardboard boxes.
examples.zh: 她在校外见到没家的人住纸板箱。

cedar.definition: n. any of numerous trees of the family Cupressaceae that resemble cedars\nn. durable aromatic wood of any of numerous cedar trees; especially wood of the red cedar often used for cedar chests\nn. any cedar of the genus Cedrus
cedar.translation: n. 雪松, 香椿\n[医] 香柏, 杉, 雪松

examples.en: They made huge, grotesque, yet beautiful poles of red cedar.
examples.zh: 他们用红雪松制作了巨大、怪诞却又美丽的木杆。

examples.en: There used to be a large cedar tree there.
examples.zh: 那里以前有一棵高大的雪松树。

examples.en: The scent of cedar repels moths.
examples.zh: 雪松的气味可以驱赶飞蛾。

centennial.definition: n. the 100th anniversary (or the celebration of it)\na. of or relating to or completing a period of 100 years
centennial.translation: n. 百年纪念\na. 一百年的

examples.en: My university is celebrating its centennial this year, so you can see banners with its colors, logo, and mascot all over the place.
examples.zh: 我的大学今年正在庆祝建校一百周年，因此你到处都可以看到带有它颜色，标志和吉祥物的横幅。

cereal.definition: n. grass whose starchy grains are used as food: wheat; rice; rye; oats; maize; buckwheat; millet\nn. a breakfast food prepared from grain\na. made of grain or relating to grain or the plants that produce it
cereal.translation: n. 谷类食品, 谷类植物\na. 谷类的

examples.en: The "complete breakfasts" in cereal commercials always include cereal, milk, toast, and orange juice, but even Americans don't usually eat that much in the morning.
examples.zh: 玉米片广告的 “完整早餐” 总有玉米片、牛奶、烤面包和橙汁，但是连美国人的早餐没有那么丰富。

chalk.definition:
n. a soft whitish calcite
n. a pure flat white with little reflectance
n. a piece of calcite or a similar substance, usually in the shape of a crayon, that is used to write or draw on blackboards or other flat surfaces
v. write, draw, or trace with chalk
chalk.translation: n. 粉笔, 白垩\nvt. 用粉笔写, 记录

examples.en: Take this piece of chalk and write on the blackboard.
examples.zh: 拿起这支粉笔，在黑板上写字。

examples.en: It is not easy to write in chalk.
examples.zh: 用粉笔写字不容易。

examples.en: Please bring me two pieces of chalk.
examples.zh: 给我拿两根粉笔来，谢谢。

champagne.definition: n. a white sparkling wine either produced in Champagne or resembling that produced there\nn. a region of northeastern France
champagne.translation: n. 香槟酒, 香槟酒色\n[化] 香槟酒

examples.en: Instead of drinking cola, why not drink champagne?
examples.zh: 与其喝可乐，倒不如喝香槟。

examples.en: This politician is a typical champagne socialist.
examples.zh: 这个政客是典型的香槟社会主义者。

examples.en: Orange juice or champagne?
examples.zh: 柳橙汁或香槟?

chaos.definition:
n. a state of extreme confusion and disorder
n. the formless and disordered state of matter before the creation of the cosmos
n. (Greek mythology) the most ancient of gods; the personification of the infinity of space preceding creation of the universe
n. (physics) a dynamical system that is extremely sensitive to its initial conditions
chaos.translation: n. 大混乱, 混沌\n[化] 混沌; 浑沌

examples.en: The world is in chaos.
examples.zh: 世界处于混沌之中。

examples.en: The accident caused traffic chaos.
examples.zh: 那场意外使交通大乱。

checkout.definition: n. the latest time for vacating a hotel room\nn. a counter in a supermarket where you pay for your purchases
checkout.translation: n. 结帐台\n[计] 检验

examples.en: Where's the checkout counter?
examples.zh: 结帐柜台在哪里?

examples.en: A brilliant, seductive chef turns to espionage in Napoleon-era France.
examples.zh: 拿破仑时代的法国，魅力诱人的天才厨师摇身一变成为间谍。

examples.en: She used to be a part time chef, then she became full time.
examples.zh: 她以前是兼职厨师，后来做了全职。

examples.en: We have a very good chef.
examples.zh: 我们有一位非常好的厨师。

chopstick.definition: n. one of a pair of slender sticks used as oriental tableware to eat food with

examples.en: We use chopsticks in place of knives and forks.
examples.zh: 我们用筷子，不用刀叉。

examples.en: Do you know how to eat with chopsticks?
examples.zh: 你会用筷子吃饭吗？

examples.en: Do you know how to correctly hold chopsticks?
examples.zh: 你知道要怎么拿筷子才是正确的吗？

chronological.definition: a. relating to or arranged according to temporal order
chronological.translation: a. 年代学的, 按时间顺序的, 按照年月顺序的\n[计] 编年的, 按年月日顺序的

examples.en: Please arrange the books on the shelves in chronological order.
Sami is telling the stories in chronological order.
The book describes the main events in his life in chronological order.

cigar.definition: n. a roll of tobacco for smoking

examples.en: Tom had a cigar in his mouth.
examples.zh: 汤姆在嘴里叼了根儿烟。

examples.en: I watched a ring of smoke that floated from his cigar into the air.
examples.zh: 我看著一轮烟圈从他的雪茄里冒出来，飘到了空气中。

examples.en: Tom lit his cigar.
examples.zh: 汤姆点了雪茄。

cipher.definition: n. a message written in a secret code\nn. a person of no influence\nn. a secret method of writing
cipher.translation: n. 零, 暗号, 密码, 无用的东西, 阿拉伯数字\nv. 计算, 做算术

examples.en: My best guess is it needs an asymmetric cipher.
Tom was writing cryptic notes in a cipher.
The information may be given in cipher.

claw.definition:
n. sharp curved horny process on the toe of a bird or some mammals or reptiles
n. a grasping structure on the limb of a crustacean or other arthropods
n. a bird's foot
v. move as if by clawing, seizing, or digging
claw.translation: n. 爪, 螯, 抓伤\nv. 用爪抓, 挖, 搜刮

examples.en: Ziri saw a large claw mark on the oak tree.
examples.zh: 齐里看到橡树上有一个很大的爪痕。

examples.en: "I cannot claw my owner", said the cat.
examples.zh: “我不能抓我的主人。”猫说。

examples.en: Animals that climb trees, like cats, have claws.
examples.zh: 爬树的动物, 比如猫, 长有爪子。

cobalt.definition: n. a hard ferromagnetic silver-white bivalent or trivalent metallic element; a trace element in plant and animal nutrition
cobalt.translation: n. 钴, 钴类颜料\n[化] 钴Co

examples.en: It's made of cobalt and nickel.
Cobalt is a transition metal.
Cobalt is a valuable mineral.

cockpit.definition: n. compartment where the pilot sits while flying the aircraft\nn. a pit for cockfights\nn. seat where the driver sits while driving a racing car
cockpit.translation: n. 驾驶员座舱, 战场

examples.en: The future pilot is trained in a mock cockpit.
examples.zh: 未来飞行员将在模拟操作室中训练。

cocoa.definition: n. a beverage made from cocoa powder and milk and sugar; usually drunk hot\nn. powder of ground roasted cacao beans with most of the fat removed
cocoa.translation: n. 可可粉, 可可茶, 可可色\n[医] 可可, 可可豆

examples.en: This chocolate factory consumes twenty metric tons of raw cocoa per day.
examples.zh: 这座巧克力工厂每一天消耗二十公吨可可原料。

examples.en: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.
examples.zh: 巧克力是用可可豆做的。

cod.definition: n. lean white flesh of important North Atlantic food fish; usually baked or poached\nn. major food fish of Arctic and cold-temperate waters
cod.translation: n. 鳕, 欺骗, 愚弄\nv. 欺骗, 愚弄

examples.en: Do you know how much a pound of cod is?
Cod fritters are delicious, but absorb lots of fat.
The Atlantic cod is the best known representative of the Gadiformes.

coma.definition: n. a state of deep and often prolonged unconsciousness; usually the result of disease or injury\nn. (botany) a usually terminal tuft of bracts (as in the pineapple) or tuft of hairs (especially on certain seeds)\nn. (astronomy) the luminous cloud of particles surrounding the frozen nucleus of a comet; forms as the comet approaches the sun and is warmed
coma.translation: n. 昏迷, 麻木, 彗发\n[化] 彗差; 彗形像差

examples.en: The patient is in a deep coma.
examples.zh: 患者现在处于深度昏迷状态。

examples.en: Unfortunately, my neighbor was involved in a traffic accident, and is currently in a coma.
examples.zh: 很不幸地，我的邻居被卷入交通事故，呈现昏迷状态。

comet.definition: n. (astronomy) a relatively small extraterrestrial body consisting of a frozen mass that travels around the sun in a highly elliptical orbit

examples.en: Halley's Comet will come back in 2061.
examples.zh: 哈雷彗星将在2061回来。

examples.en: Don't mix up comets and asteroids.
examples.zh: 不要把流星和小行星搞混了。

comic.definition: a. of or relating to or characteristic of comedy
comic.translation: n. 连环漫画, 喜剧演员, 滑稽的人\na. 滑稽的, 有趣的, 喜剧的

examples.en: The comic downloader that I wrote will be released this Sunday.
examples.zh: 我写的漫画下载器本周日就发布。

examples.en: All the characters of this comic are girls.
examples.zh: 这部漫画登场的人物全是少女。

examples.en: I borrowed this comic from his sister.
examples.zh: 我向他的妹妹借了这个漫画。

commemoration.definition: n. a ceremony to honor the memory of someone or something
commemoration.translation: n. 纪念, 纪念物, 庆典

examples.en: April 20 is not a day of festivity, it's a day of commemoration.
Both commemorations are intended to raise awareness of kidney disease and the importance of prevention and early detection.

commute.definition:
n. a regular journey of some distance to and from your place of work
v. exchange positions without a change in value
v. travel back and forth regularly, as between one's place of work and home
v. exchange a penalty for a less severe one
commute.translation: vt. 交换, 折偿, 减轻\nvi. 代偿, 经常乘车来往

examples.en: Do you commute to school by bus?
examples.zh: 你搭公车上下学吗？

examples.en: I spend a lot of time commuting.
examples.zh: 我花很多时间通勤。

compress.definition: n. a cloth pad or dressing (with or without medication) applied firmly to some part of the body (to relieve discomfort or reduce fever)\nv. make more compact by or as if by pressing\nv. squeeze or press together
compress.translation: vt. 压缩, 压紧\nvi. 受压缩小\n[计] 压缩程序

examples.en: I stomped on the pile of leaves to compress it.
Apply a compress to the affected part every two hours.
The black hole caused the ship to stretch and compress.

confession.definition:
n. an admission of misdeeds or faults
n. a written document acknowledging an offense and signed by the guilty party
n. (Roman Catholic Church) the act of a penitent disclosing his sinfulness before a priest in the sacrament of penance in the hope of absolution
n. a public declaration of your faith
confession.translation: n. 承认, 坦白, 招供\n[法] 自白, 招供, 自认有罪

examples.en: Should I make a confession of my past to her?
examples.zh: 我该不该跟她坦白我的过去？

confinement.definition: n. the act of restraining of a person's liberty by confining them\nn. the state of being confined
confinement.translation: n. 限制, 被禁闭, 分娩\n[医] 分娩, 生产

examples.en: He received her letters amidst the loneliness of solitary confinement.
His sentence of solitary confinement permanently ruined his life.
The usual date of churching was the fortieth day after confinement.

conscientious.definition: s. characterized by extreme care and great effort\na. guided by or in accordance with conscience or sense of right and wrong
conscientious.translation: a. 有责任心的, 负责的, 本着良心的\n[法] 凭良心做的, 有道德感的

examples.en: You don't seem to be as conscientious as Tom is.
Tom told me that he thought that Mary was conscientious.
Carlos is a conscientious worker who always follows safety protocols.

consonant.definition: n. a speech sound that is not a vowel\nn. a letter of the alphabet standing for a spoken consonant\ns. involving or characterized by harmony
consonant.translation: n. 辅音\na. 一致的, 调和的

examples.en: The medial consonant was difficult for the students to pronounce.
The next Berber word starts with a consonant.
A bilabial consonant is articulated with both lips.

continental.definition:
a. of or pertaining to or typical of Europe
a. of or relating to or concerning the American colonies during and immediately after the American Revolutionary War
a. of or relating to or characteristic of a continent
a. being or concerning or limited to a continent especially the continents of North America or Europe
continental.translation: a. 大陆的, 洲的\nn. 欧洲大陆人

examples.en: The Second Continental Congress governed the American colonies from 1775 to 1781.
Esther didn't have time to eat the continental breakfast.
The largest continental lake in the world is the Caspian Sea.

convent.definition: n. a religious residence especially for nuns\nn. a community of people in a religious order (especially nuns) living together
convent.translation: n. 女修道会\n[法] 召集, 召开, 开会

examples.en: Mary spent the rest of her life in a convent.
The book is about a woman who enters a convent.
Rima visited a convent in the middle of the island.

copper.definition:
n. a ductile malleable reddish-brown corrosion-resistant diamagnetic metallic element; occurs in various minerals but is the only metal that occurs abundantly in large masses; used as an electrical and thermal conductor
n. a copper penny
n. a reddish-brown color resembling the color of polished copper
n. any of various small butterflies of the family Lycaenidae having coppery wings
copper.translation: n. 铜, 警察\n[化] 铜Cu

examples.en: Now I am starting to issue copper medals.
examples.zh: 现在我开始发铜牌。

examples.en: This spoon is made of copper.
examples.zh: 这把汤匙是铜制的。

examples.en: Copper and silver are both metals.
examples.zh: 铜和银都是金属。

cork.definition:
n. outer bark of the cork oak; used for stoppers for bottles etc.
n. a port city in southern Ireland
n. the plug in the mouth of a bottle (especially a wine bottle)
v. close a bottle with a cork
cork.translation: n. 软木塞, 软木树, 软木\n[化] 木栓

examples.en: Tom had trouble getting the cork out of the bottle.
Gabriel had a piece of cork in his ear.
Do you have a cork screw I could borrow?

cornerstone.definition: n. a stone in the exterior of a large and important building; usually carved with a date and laid with appropriate ceremonies\nn. a stone at the outer corner of two intersecting masonry walls

examples.en: The means used to prepare the future become its cornerstone.
Make solidarity and equal rights the cornerstone of public policy.
Freedom of speech is the cornerstone of democracy.

corrective.definition: n. a device for treating injury or disease\ns. designed to promote discipline\ns. tending or intended to correct or counteract or restore to a normal condition
corrective.translation: a. 纠正的, 改正的, 矫正的\nn. 改善法, 矫正物

examples.en: Almost all patients require corrective eyewear after cataract surgery.
Tom sent me a corrective response, highlighting several grammatical mistakes in my message.
We must apply corrective measures.

cosy.definition: n. a padded cloth covering to keep a teapot warm
cosy.translation: a. 温暖舒适的\nn. 保暖套

examples.en: Our specialities are good plain cooking and a cosy atmosphere.
We met in the evening for a cosy get-together.
Although Tom's flat is small, it is very cosy.

countdown.definition: n. counting backward from an arbitrary number to indicate the time remaining before some event (such as launching a space vehicle)
countdown.translation: n. 倒计数\n[电] 指示串联中的操作数固定的记录减少

examples.en: Begin the launch countdown.
examples.zh: 开始发射倒数。

countless.definition: s. too numerous to be counted
countless.translation: a. 数不尽的, 无数的

examples.en: In fact, there are countless, varied uses for the Internet.
examples.zh: 实际上，网络的作用有着无数的多种多样的。

examples.en: Countless stars were twinkling in the sky.
examples.zh: 无数星星在天上闪烁。

coupon.definition: n. a negotiable certificate that can be detached and redeemed as needed\nn. a test sample of some substance
coupon.translation: n. 息票, 赠券\n[经] 息票, 利息单, 联票

examples.en: May I have coupon tickets?
examples.zh: 可以给我优惠券吗？

courteous.definition: s. exhibiting courtesy and politeness\na. characterized by courtesy and gracious good manners
courteous.translation: a. 彬彬有礼, 谦恭的

examples.en: It is very courteous of you to call on me.
Tom told me that he hoped Mary would be courteous.
Tom told me he hoped that Mary would be courteous.

coward.definition: n. a person who shows fear or timidity\nn. English dramatist and actor and composer noted for his witty and sophisticated comedies (1899-1973)
coward.translation: n. 懦弱的人, 胆小的人

examples.en: John is brave in appearance, but is in reality a coward.
examples.zh: 约翰看起来很勇敢，但其实是个胆小鬼。

examples.en: She resented being called a coward.
examples.zh: 她对被称为懦夫很反感。

examples.en: He doesn't even dare to reply to a harsh word. He's such a coward.
examples.zh: 他连一句重话都不敢回，真是个窝囊废。

crane.definition:
n. United States writer (1871-1900)
n. United States poet (1899-1932)
n. lifts and moves heavy objects; lifting tackle is suspended from a pivoted boom that rotates around a vertical axis
n. large long-necked wading bird of marshes and plains in many parts of the world
crane.translation: n. 鹤, 起重机\nvt. 伸颈, 起重机起吊\nvi. 伸颈看, 迟疑

examples.en: The crane, unlike the dog, has never dreamed of flying.
examples.zh: 不像狗, 这只鹤从来没有梦想过飞翔。

examples.en: Teach me how to fold a paper crane. I forgot how to fold it.
examples.zh: 教我怎么折纸鹤吧。我忘记怎么折了。

examples.en: Tom craned his neck in every direction.
examples.zh: 汤姆伸长脖子四处张望。

critique.definition: n an essay or article that gives a critical evaluation (as of a book or play)\nn a serious examination and judgment of something\nv appraise critically
critique.translation: n. 评论文章, 评论

examples.en: The teacher gave me a good critique on my project.
My only critique for my car was its acceleration.
Carlos's work is often the subject of peer review and critique.

crochet.definition: n. needlework done by interlocking looped stitches with a hooked needle\nv. create by looping or crocheting\nv. make a piece of needlework by interlocking and looping thread with a hooked needle
crochet.translation: n. 钩针编织品, 钩边\nv. 用钩针编织

examples.en: A new art trend in New York City takes the age-old craft of crocheting to the streets, where traditionally walls and fences have been serving as canvases for graffiti artists.
examples.zh: 纽约市出现了一种新的艺术潮流，将古老的钩编工艺带到了街头。在那里，传统上，墙壁和栅栏一直是涂鸦艺术家的画布。

crooked.definition: a. having or marked by bends or angles; not straight or aligned\na. not straight; dishonest or immoral or evasive
crooked.translation: a. 弯曲的, 歪的, 邪恶的

examples.en: Even crooked tree gives shade.
examples.zh: 即使是弯树也能遮阴。

crow.definition:
n. black birds having a raucous call
n. the cry of a cock (or an imitation of it)
n. a member of the Siouan people formerly living in eastern Montana
n. a Siouan language spoken by the Crow
crow.translation: n. 啼叫, 乌鸦, 鸡鸣, 撬棍\nvi. 啼叫, 报晓

examples.en: The crow flew away.
examples.zh: 这只乌鸦飞走了。

cruiser.definition: n. a car in which policemen cruise the streets; equipped with radiotelephonic communications to headquarters\nn. a large fast warship; smaller than a battleship and larger than a destroyer
cruiser.translation: n. 巡洋舰, 巡航飞机, 警察巡逻车

examples.en: Yanni was placed in the back of the police cruiser.
The interplanetary bank placed a lien on Tom's space cruiser.
Ziri got out of the police cruiser.

crypt.definition: n. a cellar or vault or underground burial chamber (especially beneath a church)
crypt.translation: n. 土窖, 地穴, 地下室\n[医] 隐窝; 滤泡, 腺管

examples.en: The royal crypt was pilfered by grave robbers long ago.
Donald looked like he crawled out of a crypt.
The shield you're looking for is in the crypt.

cursor.definition: n. (computer science) indicator consisting of a movable spot of light (an icon) on a visual display; moving it allows the user to point to commands or screen positions
cursor.translation: n. 游标, 光标\n[计] 光标

examples.en: Help me find the cursor. I lost sight of it.
Claudio couldn't move the cursor outside of the little window.
My cat likes to chase the mouse cursor.

cyber.translation: a. 网络的, 计算机的

examples.en: Cyber activists want to meet with the Supreme Leader.
examples.zh: 网络积极分子想跟最高领袖见面。

catalyst.definition: n. (chemistry) a substance that initiates or accelerates a chemical reaction without itself being affected\nn. something that causes an important event to happen
catalyst.translation: n. 触媒, 接触剂, 催化剂, 刺激因素, 促进因素\n[计] 催化剂

examples.en: The devastating loss became the catalyst for personal growth.
First, I'd like to examine the catalyst used in this experiment.
The catalyst system efficiency is below the threshold.

citation.definition:
n. an official award (as for bravery or service) usually given as formal public statement
n. (law) the act of citing (as of spoken words or written passages or legal precedents etc.)
n. a short note recognizing a source of information or of a quoted passage
n. a summons that commands the appearance of a party at a proceeding
citation.translation: n. 引用, 引证, 引用文\n[建] 引证, 指引

examples.en: Academic writing should contain facts supported by citation.
His criminal record consists of only two drunken driving citations.
Tom's criminal record consists of only two drunken driving citations.

cavern.definition: n. any large dark enclosed space\nn. a large cave or a large chamber in a cave\nv. hollow out as if making a cavern
cavern.translation: n. 巨穴, 洞窟, 深处\nvt. 放于山洞中, 挖空

examples.en: A dragon lives inside the cavern.
examples.zh: 一条龙住在洞穴里。

cinnamon.definition: n. aromatic bark used as a spice\nn. tropical Asian tree with aromatic yellowish-brown bark; source of the spice cinnamon\nn. spice from the dried aromatic bark of the Ceylon cinnamon tree; used as rolled strips or ground
cinnamon.translation: n. 肉桂, 肉桂树皮, 肉桂色\na. 肉桂色的, 浅黄褐色的

examples.en: Tom likes tea with cinnamon.
examples.zh: 汤姆喜欢喝加肉桂的茶。

colonel.definition: n. a commissioned military officer in the United States Army or Air Force or Marines who ranks above a lieutenant colonel and below a brigadier general
colonel.translation: n. 陆军上校, 长官

examples.en: He advanced to colonel.
examples.zh: 他晋升为大佐。

calculus.definition: n. a hard lump produced by the concretion of mineral salts; found in hollow organs or ducts of the body\nn. the branch of mathematics that is concerned with limits and with the differentiation and integration of functions

examples.en: Last year I was a TA for calculus.
examples.zh: 去年我是一个微积分学助教。

examples.en: The integral and the antiderivative are defined in two different ways, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus states the relationship between them.
examples.zh: 积分与反导函数是以两种不同的方式定义的，而微积分基本定理阐述了两者之间的关系。

constellation.definition: n. a configuration of stars as seen from the earth
constellation.translation: n. 星座, 荟萃\n[化] 构象

examples.en: I count the sparkle of constellations to foretell the future of my love.
examples.zh: 我数著星宿的星光来预测我爱情的未来。

cyclone.definition: n. (meteorology) rapid inward circulation of air masses about a low pressure center; circling counterclockwise in the northern hemisphere and clockwise in the southern\nn. a violent rotating windstorm
cyclone.translation: n. 龙卷风, 暴风\n[化] 旋流(分离,除尘)器

examples.en: Many houses in my village have been destroyed by the cyclone.
The cyclone destroyed everything in its path.
The cyclone had given the unbroken house to a land of divine beauty.

cashew.definition: n. tropical American evergreen tree bearing kidney-shaped nuts that are edible only when roasted\nn. kidney-shaped nut edible only when roasted
cashew.translation: n. 腰果树, 腰果\n[化] ┐如树; 腰果树

examples.en: How much is one box of cashew turrones?
I want to drink cashew juice.
He had a late night snack of cheese, cashews, and German natural herb bitters.

celery.definition: n. widely cultivated herb with aromatic leaf stalks that are eaten raw or cooked\nn. stalks eaten raw or cooked or used as seasoning
celery.translation: n. 芹菜\n[医] 芹菜, 糖蒿

examples.en: In this soup there are carrots, onions, parsley, celery and potatoes.
examples.zh: 这个汤里有胡萝卜、洋葱、欧芹、芹菜和土豆。

examples.en: Tableland vegetables are grown here, such as lettuce, cabbage, and celery.
examples.zh: 这里种植有生菜、高丽菜和芹菜等高原蔬菜。

examples.en: I am peeling the celery and the potatoes.
examples.zh: 我在削芹菜和土豆。

coconut.definition: n. the edible white meat of a coconut; often shredded for use in e.g. cakes and curries\nn. large hard-shelled oval nut with a fibrous husk containing thick white meat surrounding a central cavity filled (when fresh) with fluid or milk\nn. tall palm tree bearing coconuts as fruits; widely planted throughout the tropics
coconut.translation: n. 椰子\n[医] 椰子(实)

examples.en: The London to Amsterdam flight was partially powered with a mixture of coconut and babassu nut oil.
examples.zh: 伦敦飞往阿姆斯特丹的航班部分动力来自椰子油和巴巴苏坚果油的混合物。

cranberry.definition: n. any of numerous shrubs of genus Vaccinium bearing cranberries\nn. very tart red berry used for sauce or juice

examples.en: We like to eat fresh cranberries.
examples.zh: 我们喜欢吃新鲜的小红莓。

cucumber.definition: n. a melon vine of the genus Cucumis; cultivated from earliest times for its cylindrical green fruit\nn. cylindrical green fruit with thin green rind and white flesh eaten as a vegetable; related to melons
cucumber.translation: n. 黄瓜\n[医] 黄瓜, 胡瓜

examples.en: She has a cucumber at her bedside.
examples.zh: 她床头有一根黄瓜。

examples.en: A horse doesn't eat cucumber salad.
examples.zh: 马不吃黄瓜沙拉。

examples.en: This cucumber is very long!
examples.zh: 这根黄瓜好长啊！

cheetah.definition: n. long-legged spotted cat of Africa and southwestern Asia having nonretractile claws; the swiftest mammal; can be trained to run down game

examples.en: A cheetah can run as fast as 70 miles per hour.
The cheetah is very closely related to the domestic cat.
The Saharan cheetah is perhaps the rarest cat in Algeria.

cobra.definition: n. venomous Asiatic and African elapid snakes that can expand the skin of the neck into a hood
cobra.translation: n. 眼镜蛇\n[医] 眼镜蛇

examples.en: I heard that Tom was bitten by a cobra.
What should you do if you are bitten by a cobra?
Tom died three weeks ago after being bitten by a cobra.

cello.definition: n. a large stringed instrument; seated player holds it upright while playing

examples.en: I thought you said your cello was in the car.
I don't think Tom knows how to play the cello.
Tom doesn't play the cello as well as Mary does.

clarinet.definition: n. a single-reed instrument with a straight tube
clarinet.translation: n. 竖笛, 单簧管, 黑管

examples.en: Neither Tom nor Mary knows how to play the clarinet.
examples.zh: 汤姆和玛丽都不会吹单簧管。

cymbal.definition: n. a percussion instrument consisting of a concave brass disk; makes a loud crashing sound when hit with a drumstick or when two are struck together

examples.en: The goddess has a cymbal in her hands.
The cymbals are harder to play than one might think.
The cymbal is a percussion instrument.

capitalism.definition: n. an economic system based on private ownership of capital
capitalism.translation: n. 资本主义\n[经] 资本主义

examples.en: Capitalism is poverty.
examples.zh: 资本主义是贫穷。

cartoon.definition: n. a humorous or satirical drawing published in a newspaper or magazine\nn. a film made by photographing a series of cartoon drawings to give the illusion of movement when projected in rapid sequence\nv. draw cartoons of
cartoon.translation: n. 卡通画, 漫画\nv. 画漫画

examples.en: Some people say that cartoons on television are educational in themselves.
examples.zh: 有人说电视上的卡通本身是有教育意义的。

examples.en: Do you know this cartoon?
examples.zh: 你知道这部漫画吗？

choke.definition:
n. a coil of low resistance and high inductance used in electrical circuits to pass direct current and attenuate alternating current
n. a valve that controls the flow of air into the carburetor of a gasoline engine
v. breathe with great difficulty, as when experiencing a strong emotion
v. be too tight; rub or press
choke.translation: vt. 窒息, 阻塞, 噎, 抑制\nvi. 窒息, 阻塞, 噎\nn. 窒息, 噎, 阻气门

examples.en: Let me go, you're choking me.
examples.zh: 放开我，你正在掐着我的脖子。

examples.en: I'm getting choked up.
examples.zh: 我快要激动得说不出话来了。

comparative.definition: n. the comparative form of an adjective or adverb\na. relating to or based on or involving comparison
comparative.translation: a. 比较的, 相对的\nn. 对手

examples.en: I study comparative religion in the arts faculty of the University of Turku.
examples.zh: 我在图尔库大学文化系学习宗教比较学。

examples.en: My major is comparative religion.
examples.zh: 我的专业是宗教学。

confer.definition: v. have a conference in order to talk something over\nv. present
confer.translation: vt. 授予, 带来\nvi. 协商

examples.en: Minds that have nothing to confer find little to perceive.
If purchase does not confer ownership, then piracy isn't theft.
I must confer with my colleagues on the matter.

constitutional.definition: n. a regular walk taken as a form of exercise\na. of benefit to or intended to benefit your physical makeup\na. sanctioned by or consistent with or operating under the law determining the fundamental political principles of a government
constitutional.translation: a. 宪法的, 立宪的, 体质的\n[医] 全身的; 体质的

examples.en: Sami has a constitutional right not to take the stand.
The constitutional court will issue a decision by noon today.
America has an elaborate system of constitutional checks and balances.

calculating.translation: a. 计算的, (贬)专为自己打算的, 深谋远虑的\n[计] 计算

examples.en: The first calculating tool of mankind is called an abacus.
Computers can be thought of as mere calculating machines.
Primitive calculating machines existed long before computers were developed.

candidacy.definition: n the campaign of a candidate to be elected
candidacy.translation: n. 候选人的地位, 候选资格\n[法] 候选人的身份, 资格

examples.en: We took the liberty of putting your candidacy on hold.
No one expected him to announce his candidacy again.
I'm here to announce my candidacy for Congress.

cane.definition:
n. a stick that people can lean on to help them walk
n. a strong slender often flexible stem as of bamboos, reeds, rattans, or sugar cane
n. a stiff switch used to hit students as punishment
v. beat with a cane
cane.translation: n. 手杖, 细长的茎, 藤条\nvt. 以杖击, 以藤编制

examples.en: Sugar cane is sweet.
examples.zh: 甘蔗是甜的。

examples.en: Thoreau coveted the plant's strong purple stalk for a cane, and the robins eat its dark crimson-juiced berries.
examples.zh: 梭罗垂涎于这种植物强壮的紫色茎秆，将其制成藤条，而知更鸟则以深红色汁液的浆果为食。

cannon.definition:
n. a large artillery gun that is usually on wheels
n. heavy gun fired from a tank
n. (Middle Ages) a cylindrical piece of armor plate to protect the arm
n. heavy automatic gun fired from an airplane
cannon.translation: n. 大炮, 加农炮\nv. 炮轰

examples.en: Never use a cannon to kill a fly.
examples.zh: 杀鸡焉用牛刀。

canoe.definition: n. small and light boat; pointed at both ends; propelled with a paddle\nv. travel by canoe
canoe.translation: n. 独木舟, 轻舟\nvi. 乘独木舟\nvt. 用独木舟运

examples.en: We went down a river by canoe.
examples.zh: 我们乘著独木舟向河的下游而行。

examples.en: We rented a canoe.
examples.zh: 我们租了一艘划艇。

capability.definition: n. the quality of being capable -- physically or intellectually or legally\nn. the susceptibility of something to a particular treatment\nn. an aptitude that may be developed
capability.translation: n. 能力, 性能, 约束力\n[化] 能力

examples.en: My classmate, Xiao Ming, has strong managerial capability.
examples.zh: 小明同学管理能力很强。

carbohydrate.definition: n. an essential structural component of living cells and source of energy for animals; includes simple sugars with small molecules as well as macromolecular substances; are classified according to the number of monosaccharide groups they contain
carbohydrate.translation: n. 碳水化合物, 糖类\n[化] 糖类; 碳水化合物

examples.en: Do you know anything about complex carbohydrates?
examples.zh: 你对复合碳水化合物有什么了解吗？

carton.definition: n. the quantity contained in a carton\nn. a box made of cardboard; opens by flaps on top
carton.translation: n. 硬纸盒, 纸板箱\n[化] 卡纸

examples.en: Robert dropped an entire carton of milk all over Linda's head.
examples.zh: 罗伯将一整盒牛奶洒在琳达头上。

carving.definition: n. a sculpture created by removing material (as wood or ivory or stone) in order to create a desired shape\nn. removing parts from hard material to create a desired pattern or shape
carving.translation: n. 雕刻品, 雕刻, 雕刻术

examples.en: This carving knife ... it's one made by a famous swordsmith.
The river knows no bounds, carving its own path.
Jonas came into Amelia's room with a carving knife.

casino.definition: n. a public building for gambling and entertainment\nn. a card game in which cards face up on the table are taken with eligible cards in the hand
casino.translation: n. 卡西诺赌场, 卡西诺牌戏

examples.en: After three hours in the casino, he's $2,000 in the hole.
Tom won a lot of money at the casino.
Tom lost a lot of money at the casino.

catastrophic.definition: s. extremely harmful; bringing physical or financial ruin
catastrophic.translation: a. 悲惨的, 灾难的

examples.en: This could have more catastrophic results as time goes on.
Ziri and Rima's relationship is going to a catastrophic end.
Ziri and Rima's relationship is gonna have a catastrophic end.

cauliflower.definition: n. a plant having a large edible head of crowded white flower buds\nn. compact head of white undeveloped flowers
cauliflower.translation: n. 花椰菜\n[医] 花椰菜(菜花)

examples.en: When I eat cauliflower or drink milk, I fart.
Here is a recipe for which cauliflower is necessary.
Cauliflower is nothing but cabbage with a college education.

cavity.definition: n. space that is surrounded by something\nn. soft decayed area in a tooth; progressive decay can lead to the death of a tooth\nn. (anatomy) a natural hollow or sinus within the body
cavity.translation: n. 洞, 空穴, 腔\n[化] 空穴

examples.en: Mary got a cavity because she never brushes her teeth.
Mennad went to the dentist's to have his cavity filled.
Sami has never had a cavity in his life.

censorship.definition: n counterintelligence achieved by banning or deleting any information of value to the enemy\nn deleting parts of publications or correspondence or theatrical performances
censorship.translation: n. 检查制度\n[医] 督察, 监察

examples.en: If you support banning foreign languages, you don't oppose censorship.
The Melbourne police raided the bookstore for violating censorship laws.
Treating disagreement as censorship is a pretext to censor disagreement.

certify.definition: v. guarantee payment on; of checks\nv. guarantee as meeting a certain standard\nv. declare legally insane

examples.en: John is a certified Apple fanboy.
examples.zh: 约翰是认证果粉。

examples.en: Ziri became a certified online teacher.
examples.zh: 齐莉成为了认证线上教师。

examples.en: Bruno is board certified in psychiatry.
examples.zh: 布鲁诺是委员会认证的精神科专家。

chairperson.definition: n the officer who presides at the meetings of an organization

examples.en: We elected her chairperson.
examples.zh: 我们选她为主席。

examples.en: Mike was elected chairperson.
examples.zh: 迈克当选为主席。

examples.en: She was appointed chairperson.
examples.zh: 她被任命为主席。

challenging.definition: s. stimulating interest or thought\ns. disturbingly provocative
challenging.translation: a. 挑战的, 引起争论的

examples.en: We express our gratitude for Mr Smith's outstanding, challenging speech.
examples.zh: 我们对史密斯先生杰出的，给人启发的讲话表示感激。

examples.en: Tom likes challenging himself.
examples.zh: 汤姆喜欢挑战自己。

chaotic.definition: s. lacking a visible order or organization\ns. completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing\na. of or relating to a sensitive dependence on initial conditions
chaotic.translation: a. 混乱的, 无秩序的\n[法] 混乱的, 混沌的

examples.en: The kine was very chaotic and they all died.
Fadil was raised by a single mother in a chaotic household.
You think that I'm chaotic, but I'm versatile.

charming.definition: s. pleasing or delighting\ns. possessing or using or characteristic of or appropriate to supernatural powers
charming.translation: a. 迷人的, 有吸引力的

examples.en: She never wears makeup, but she always looks very charming.
examples.zh: 她从不化妆, 但总是看起来很迷人。

examples.en: He thought of himself as being charming enough.
examples.zh: 他认为他自己够迷人的了。

examples.en: She thought of herself as being charming enough.
examples.zh: 她认为她自己够迷人的了。

childish.definition: s. indicating a lack of maturity
childish.translation: a. 天真的, 孩子气的

examples.en: It is time you left off your childish ways.
examples.zh: 是你该放弃你幼稚手段的时候了。

examples.en: His way of thinking is very childish.
examples.zh: 他的思维方式很幼稚。

examples.en: Don't be so childish.
examples.zh: 不要那么幼稚。

chilly.definition: s. not characterized by emotion\ns. appreciably or disagreeably cold\ns. lacking warmth of feeling
chilly.translation: a. 寒冷的, 冷淡的, 不友好的\n[建] 番椒, 冷

examples.en: It's a little chilly in here.
examples.zh: 这里有点寒冷。

examples.en: It's a chilly morning.
examples.zh: 这是一个寒冷的早晨。

china.definition: n. a communist nation that covers a vast territory in eastern Asia; the most populous country in the world\nn. high quality porcelain originally made only in China
china.translation: n. 中国, 瓷器\na. 中国的

examples.en: The history of China is older than that of Japan.
examples.zh: 中国历史比日本历史更悠久。

examples.en: Algeria is a close ally of both Russia and China.
examples.zh: 阿尔及利亚是俄罗斯和中国的亲密盟友。

examples.en: The last time I went to China, I visited Shanghai.
examples.zh: 我上次去过了中国，我访问了上海。

choir.definition:
n. a chorus that sings as part of a religious ceremony
n. a family of similar musical instrument playing together
n. the area occupied by singers; the part of the chancel between sanctuary and nave
v. sing in a choir
choir.translation: n. 唱诗班, 唱诗班的席位\nv. 合唱

examples.en: Are you still in the choir?
examples.zh: 你还在合唱团里面吗？

choosy.translation: a. 慎重选择的, 好挑剔的

examples.en: No women like to wear a dress that another discarded. With men, they're not so choosy.
examples.zh: 没有女人会喜欢穿二手裙子；可是二手男人呢，她们却照要不误。

chorus.definition:
n. any utterance produced simultaneously by a group
n. a group of people assembled to sing together
n. a body of dancers or singers who perform together
n. a company of actors who comment (by speaking or singing in unison) on the action in a classical Greek play
chorus.translation: n. 合唱队, 齐声\nv. 齐声说道, 合唱

examples.en: I did not listen to the chorus of that song.
Tom sang with a men's chorus for many years.
We tried hard to get first prize in the chorus contest.

chronically.definition: r. in a habitual and longstanding manner\nr. in a slowly developing and long lasting manner
chronically.translation: adv. 慢性地, 长期地, 习惯性地

examples.en: Yanni has become chronically homeless.
Police districts are chronically understaffed.
Sami was chronically unemployed.

chronicle.definition: v. record in chronological order; make a historical record
chronicle.translation: n. 年代记, 记录, 编年史\nvt. 把...载入编年史

examples.en: Resumes are a simple way to chronicle our vocational training.
The Sacramento Chronicle writes frequently about that old trapper.
This medieval chronicle reccords the major battles of the 13th century.

clarification.definition: n. an interpretation that removes obstacles to understanding
clarification.translation: n. 澄清, 净化\n[计] 澄清报告; 澄清

examples.en: Thank you for the clarification.
examples.zh: 感谢澄清。

examples.en: Thanks for the clarification.
examples.zh: 感谢澄清。

clarity.definition: n. free from obscurity and easy to understand; the comprehensibility of clear expression
clarity.translation: n. 清楚, 明晰\n[化] 透明度; 透明性; 清晰性

examples.en: All individuals in the world act with clear goals and distinct intentions. But once these actions are brought together by the great torrents of life, clarity recedes and chaos ensues.
examples.zh: 世界上任何人的独自活动，都是清醒而目标明确的，然而一旦被生活的洪流聚在一起，就变得混沌不清了。

classification.definition: n. a group of people or things arranged by class or category\nn. the basic cognitive process of arranging into classes or categories\nn. restriction imposed by the government on documents or weapons that are available only to certain authorized people
classification.translation: n. 分类, 分级\n[化] 分级; 分粒; 分类

examples.en: Not every racist country has the same racial classification system.
The first biologists worked hard towards the classification of living things.
Support vector machines are supervised learning models used for classification and regression analysis.

classified.definition: a. arranged into classes\na. official classification of information or documents; withheld from general circulation
classified.translation: a. 分类的, 被归入某类的, 被指定为机密的\n[建] 分了类的, 分了级的

examples.en: The classified ad wanted female singers to form an a cappella group.
examples.zh: 这则分类广告招募女歌手组成无伴奏合唱团。

examples.en: The classified documents were hidden.
examples.zh: 机密文件被藏起来了。

examples.en: Data compression algorithms can be classified in two categories: those with data loss and those without data loss.
examples.zh: 压缩数据的算法能分为两种：一种会造成数据损失，另一种则不会。

cleanse.definition: v. clean one's body or parts thereof, as by washing\nv. purge of an ideology, bad thoughts, or sins
cleanse.translation: vt. 使清洁, 净化, 使纯净\n[建] 纯化, 净化, 精炼

examples.en: He cleansed the wound before putting on a bandage.
examples.zh: 他先清洗了伤口，再绑上绷带。

clearing.definition: n. a tract of land with few or no trees in the middle of a wooded area\nn. the act of freeing from suspicion\nn. the act of removing solid particles from a liquid
clearing.translation: n. 清扫, 空地, 票据清算\n[经] 票据交换, 结算, 结帐

examples.en: Fortunately, my wound is clearing up quickly.
examples.zh: 幸运的是我的伤口消失得很快。

examples.en: Tom is clearing the garden.
examples.zh: 汤姆正在清理花园。

clench.definition: v. hold in a tight grasp\nv. squeeze together tightly
clench.translation: n. 牢牢抓住, 钉紧, 敲弯钉尖\nvt. 紧握, 牢牢地抓住, 确定, 敲弯\nvi. 握紧, 钉牢

examples.en: Tom clenched his fists.
examples.zh: 汤姆握紧了他的拳头。

examples.en: Tom clenched his teeth.
examples.zh: 汤姆咬紧牙关。

examples.en: Tom clenched the shovel.
examples.zh: 汤姆握紧了铲子。

clerical.definition: a. of or relating to clerks\na. of or relating to the clergy\ns. appropriate for or engaged in office work
clerical.translation: n. 牧师\na. 文书的, 事务上的, 抄写员的, 牧师的

examples.en: I find it so strange that keyboards can be both musical and clerical.
Maybe Tom made a clerical error.
After World War II, many employers hired women as temporary workers in clerical jobs.

climatic.definition: a. of or relating to a climate

examples.en: What do we know about the climatic history of Mars?
By the 27th century, weather and climatic control became perfected.
Environmental pollution triggered climatic changes all over Earth.

climax.definition:
n. the highest point of anything conceived of as growing or developing or unfolding
n. the decisive moment in a novel or play
n. the most severe stage of a disease
n. arrangement of clauses in ascending order of forcefulness
climax.translation: n. 高潮, 极点, 层进法\nv. (使)达到顶点, (使)达到高潮

examples.en: I am reaching the climax.
examples.zh: 我快要到高潮了。

cloak.definition: n. anything that covers or conceals\nn. a loose outer garment\nv. cover with or as if with a cloak
cloak.translation: n. 斗蓬, 大氅, 掩护\nvt. 遮掩, 隐匿, 使披斗蓬

examples.en: Under the cloak of anonymity, cowards are acting like bigmouths.
Help me on with my cloak, and hand me my sword-belt.
Ziri enjoyed the playful tug of the breeze at his cloak.

clog.definition:
n. footwear usually with wooden soles
n. any object that acts as a hindrance or obstruction
v. become or cause to become obstructed
v. dance a clog dance
clog.translation: n. 障碍, 脚坠\nv. 障碍, 阻塞

examples.en: Sami's sink got clogged.
examples.zh: 萨米的洗脸盆塞住了。

examples.en: The toilets are clogged.
examples.zh: 厕所塞住了。

clothe.definition: v. cover as if with clothing
clothe.translation: vt. 给...穿衣, 盖上, 赋予

examples.en: He plunged into the lake fully clothed.
examples.zh: 他连衣服也没有脱就跳进了湖里。

coexist.definition: v. coexist peacefully, as of nations\nv. exist together

examples.en: I know the human being and fish can coexist peacefully.
Gandhi wanted to make Hindus and Muslims coexist peacefully.
Ziri wanted to figure out how science and religion could coexist.

coexistence.translation: n. 共存, 和平共处, 并立

examples.en: "Peaceful" coexistence and multiculturalism: racism's best hiding place in Eleusis.
We successfully achieved a state of peaceful coexistence.
We aren't born with the capacity to carry out a happy coexistence.

cognition.definition: n. the psychological result of perception and learning and reasoning
cognition.translation: n. 认识, 认识力, 认识的结果\n[医] 认识, 识别

coherence.definition: n. the state of cohering or sticking together\nn. logical and orderly and consistent relation of parts
coherence.translation: n. 黏合(性), 连贯性, 一致性\n[化] 相干性

examples.en: Academic writing needs to show cohesion and coherence.
He regained a little coherence.
We recognize coherence in texts.

cohesion.definition: n. (botany) the process in some plants of parts growing together that are usually separate (such as petals)\nn. (physics) the intermolecular force that holds together the molecules in a solid or liquid
cohesion.translation: n. 结合, 黏聚, 内聚\n[计] 内聚性

examples.en: Academic writing needs to show cohesion and coherence.
He speaks without meaning or cohesion.
Grooming in primates increases group cohesion.

cohesive.definition: s. causing cohesion\ns. cohering or tending to cohere; well integrated
cohesive.translation: a. 黏合在一起的\n[医] 内聚的

examples.en: A text could be coherent but not cohesive, and vice versa.
None of those thoughts are cohesive nor do they make sense independently.
The departmental heads, lost in petty argument, could not reach a cohesive decision.

coinage.translation: n. 造币\n[经] 造币, 货币制度

examples.en: I should really figure out the coinage in this country.
Eric who was a weak prince issued a bad coinage which excited great discontent among the Danes.

collide.definition: v. cause to collide\nv. crash together with violent impact
collide.translation: vi. 碰撞, 互撞, 抵触

examples.en: Making protons collide is what the Large Hadron Collider does.
Dmitri and Rima’s arms collide when they write.
Egoists do not meet, they collide with each other.

colon.definition:
n. the part of the large intestine between the cecum and the rectum; it extracts moisture from food residues before they are excreted
n. the basic unit of money in El Salvador; equal to 100 centavos
n. the basic unit of money in Costa Rica; equal to 100 centimos
n. a port city at the Caribbean entrance to the Panama Canal
colon.translation: n. 冒号, 结肠\n[医] 结肠

examples.en: Tom was diagnosed with colon cancer in October of 2013.
They say nitrite is harmful to the colon.
Bogdan Tanevich is retiring due to colon cancer.

comma.definition: n. a punctuation mark (,) used to indicate the separation of elements within the grammatical structure of a sentence\nn. anglewing butterfly with a comma-shaped mark on the underside of each hind wing

examples.en: I'm only going to write small sentences without commas.
examples.zh: 我只是想写一些没有逗号的小句子。

commence.definition: v take the first step or steps in carrying out an action\nv set in motion, cause to start\nv get off the ground

examples.en: The conference will commence in due course.
The drilling operation is about to commence.
When will you commence the construction work?

commencement.definition: n. an academic exercise in which diplomas are conferred
commencement.translation: n. 开始, 毕业典礼\n[法] 开始, 毕业典礼

examples.en: Commencement is typically the first or second Saturday in April.
Tom gave the commencement address.
This event, also called commencement, is where schools recognize the students who successfully completed their degree programs.

commonwealth.definition: n. the official name of some states in the United States (Massachusetts and Pennsylvania and Virginia and Kentucky) and associated territories (Puerto Rico)\nn. a world organization of autonomous states that are united in allegiance to a central power but are not subordinate to it or to one another
commonwealth.translation: n. 共和国；联邦；国民整体

examples.en: The British Commonwealth of Nations is unable to let go of power.
Bangladesh joined the Commonwealth of Nations in 1972 and the United Nations in 1974.
Barbados is a member of the Commonwealth.

companionship.definition: n the state of being with someone
companionship.translation: n. 交往, 友谊, 一群同伴

examples.en: "Ziri offers companionship." "What do you mean?" "He provides escorts."
Friends offer companionship that is built on mutual respect.
Mating can be more about companionship than reproduction.

compassionate.translation: a. 慈悲的, 富于同情心的, 照顾性的\nvt. 怜悯, 同情

examples.en: Tom isn't as compassionate as he used to be.
I know that Tom is a very compassionate person.
My parents taught me to be a compassionate person.
